findings.section: §12.2 sep-build.js sketch (rows 5, 15, 17 of §6); §5.1 `calls` cap
findings.claim: The reference control loop implements 'RE-RUN S7', 'JUDGE→fix' and 'refuted HOLD' with `round--; continue` / fall-through, which re-runs the executor or parks the unit under a non-existent target, so a harness hiccup deterministically ends at H3.
findings.scenario: T1 unit U1, round 0: executor pass, gate pass, inspector pass, sandbox built, cold lens returns evidence=[] → decide() = 'rerun-blind' → sketch does `round--; continue` → loop top calls `agent(execPrompt(epic,u,cards,sha))` with an IDENTICAL prompt (cards still []). Either the run cache replays the same evidence → `ev.diff_sha256 === st.lastHash` → `return {u, stuck:'no-progress'}` → H3 stuck card + descendants blocked, caused by one lens not executing; or a second executor re-implements from base_sha → new diff → gate/S6 re-run (≈5 extra calls) and the artifact S6 approved is silently replaced. Same loop: row 17 judge says `fix` → `d.action` stays 'judge' → `return {u, sendback:'judge'}` (no such stage; unit parked). Row 15: verifier REFUTES the hazard → `if (!v.refuted)` skipped → falls to `return {u, sendback:'hold'}` → refuted hazard parks the unit. Also `st.calls++` counts only executors while the sketch spends 5 agent calls on the T0 happy path (executor, gate-runner, sandbox-runner, cold lens, M-judge) against a §5.1 cap of 4: under the §5.1 reading every T0 unit trips row 1 on its first retry.
findings.fix: Rewrite the per-unit loop as an explicit state machine `stage ∈ {execute, gate, inspect, sandbox, blind, decide}`; 'rerun-blind' sets stage='sandbox' (never re-executes); judge `fix` sets `d.action='execute', cards=j.defects`; a refuted hold sets H=0 and re-evaluates decide(); assert `sendback ∈ {execute,contract,decompose,intake}` else throw a harness error. Define `calls` as LLM stage calls only (executor/inspector/lens/judge/verifier-for-hold); utility runs (gate.sh, sandbox.sh, ratchet.sh via sep-verifier) are not counted, and the self-test asserts the T0 happy path + one blind re-run stays under cap.

findings.section: §6 decision table rows 10, 13, 14, 16, 19–21
findings.claim: Realistic input combinations match no row (unit left in an undefined state) and rows 14, 20, 21 are shadowed by earlier rows, so the T0 promotion path never runs.
findings.scenario: (a) T1: G=pass,S=yes,I=pass,Bc=PASS,Bk=UNSAFE with a claim at file:line but no runnable repro and no hazard class ('breaks on Windows paths'),M=MATCH,H=0,R=green → rows 1–16 no, 17 is T2+ only, 19 needs Bk∈{SAFE,skipped}, 20–22 no → decide.sh returns nothing; the sketch pushes `undefined`, the wave barrier waits forever or the unit is parked with no card. (b) library zone `run: null`, customer lens wrote its 10-line program, one AC UNVERIFIABLE (needs an external service), H=0 → row 13 says '→ row 15' but row 15 needs H>0 → no row. (c) Bk=ILLEGIBLE plus one concern note → row 16's 'no other finding' is false → rows 17–22 miss → no row. (d) T0 unit, cold lens block WITH repro → row 10 ('any blind block with repro') matches first, so row 21 (PROMOTE to T1 + S6 + customer lens) is dead: the unit is re-executed as T0 (sendbacks.execute cap 1) with no S6; a second cold block → row 1 → H3 stuck card for a typo-class unit. Row 14 is shadowed by 10, row 20 by 19.
findings.fix: (i) Normalize at the S7 exit gate before decide.sh: UNSAFE without repro and without hazard → verdict rewritten to SAFE with the findings kept as `concern` (log `downgraded:true` for §11 precision); a per-AC FAIL with no command → UNVERIFIABLE. (ii) Row 13: `Bc=UNVERIFIABLE` on an AC covered by a passing contract check → PASS-by-contract; otherwise, when run==null → HOLD (row 22 semantics); only when run≠null → S0. (iii) Row 16: 'no other BLOCKING finding'. (iv) Move row 21 above row 10 as 'class T0 and any blind block with repro → PROMOTE T1, ratchet, then row 10'; delete rows 14 and 20. (v) Add a terminal row 23 'anything else → ESCALATE H3 "table gap" + harness incident' and make selftest.sh enumerate the full G×S×I×Bc×Bk×M×H×R×L×E cross-product asserting every tuple hits a row < 23.

findings.section: §3 S8 Integration; §8.5; §6 row 18
findings.claim: A wave-level regression (full gate red after all units landed on the append-only integration branch) has no attribution rule, so nothing can be sent back and the next wave is built on a red base, cascading into H3 for every downstream unit.
findings.scenario: T1 wave U1..U4, all MERGE verdicts; each lands after a clean `merge-tree` dry-run; the repo `full` command runs once per wave → red (U2 renamed a helper U4 calls; each green alone). R=regression, but row 18 sends 'S5 rebase task with the conflict list' charged per PAIR — there is no textual conflict and no pair. `integration` is append-only, so all four stay. S3 for wave 2 re-checks contracts RED-on-base against the red tip; wave-2 executors' zone `full` is red for reasons outside their write-set → G=fail → exec_retries → S2 → `sendbacks.decompose` cap → H3 for each wave-2 unit, while nothing identifies U2/U4.
findings.fix: On a red wave gate the script bisects by landing order with append-only revert commits (revert last, run full, …); the first revert that turns the gate green identifies the culprit, its revert stays, and that unit gets an S5 task 'make full green on integration tip' charged to `integration_rounds[unit]` (cap 2 per UNIT, not per pair). If no single revert cures it, revert the whole wave and raise one H3 naming the units. Record `state.json.integration_red=true`, and S3 refuses to dispatch any wave while it is set.

findings.section: §12.2 (driver args, inputs_sha, sketch wave loop); §5.5 'nothing green is re-run'; §5.1 counters per unit
findings.claim: A relaunch after H3 is a new run whose prompts embed a changed global inputs hash, so every merged unit is re-executed and collides with itself on integration; and replanned children get fresh unit ids with zeroed counters, so the decompose cap never trips.
findings.scenario: Waves [[U1,U2],[U3]]: U1 merged, U2 parked at H3 (sendbacks.execute exhausted), U3 blocked. Human adds ruling R7 → rulings.md changes → `sha` changes → driver relaunches sep-build.js with `args:{epic, ts, answers_sha}` and the full schedule. No prompt is cache-hit; the loop iterates wave 1 again → U1's executor runs in a fresh worktree from base_sha → new diff → gate/S6/S7 (≈5 calls) → integrator merges U1' onto an integration that already contains U1 → conflict → row 18 rebase task → conflict again → 'serialize + H3'. One human touch created a second H3 on a green unit. Separately: U2 → sendback 'decompose' → planner emits U2a/U2b as new ids → `state.json.units[U2a].sendbacks.decompose = 0` → U2a can replan again → U2a1 … the T1 cap of 1 never fires; only the 14-day lifetime ends it. (Note §5.1 says counters live in state.json 'incremented by scripts' while §12.2 says scripts have no filesystem access — the persistence path is undefined.)
findings.fix: Driver filters `waves` by `state.json.units[u].merged` and passes per-unit resume state; the script asserts it never dispatches a merged unit. `inputs_sha` is per unit (hash of card, contract, tests, and only the rulings whose [epic/unit] tag matches), not a global hash. On replan, children carry `parent` and inherit the parent's `sendbacks.*`, `sigs_seen`, `calls`; caps are evaluated on the subtree root. State the persistence contract: the script returns `counters` in its JSON and the driver writes state.json atomically after every script return.

findings.section: §6 row 4; §2.1 'runs every skipped stage'; §3 S5 gate; §12.2 promote()
findings.claim: Promotion re-runs S2/S4/H1 for a unit that already has a diff while its siblings are mid-pipeline, with no rule for what happens to the diff, the DAG, or the human boundary, and the re-run S2 is uncounted.
findings.scenario: T0 'fix typo in error message', synthesized card, 1 file. The executor also edits `auth/session.go` through a Bash sed (guard-bash is best-effort; gate.sh is authoritative) → class_actual=T2 (risk path). Row 4: run S0 premortem, S2 planner+auditor, S4 two spikes+contract-checker, H1 (human), 2 inspectors, 3 lenses. Open questions the spec leaves: the planner returns a new dag.json — for this unit or the epic? If it splits the unit or changes write-sets, the S2 disjointness gate is checked against a DAG that no longer contains the sibling units currently executing in the pipeline → overlap unchecked → row 18 later. Is S5 re-run with the new frozen acceptance test or only the gate? H1 is a human boundary inside sep-build.js, which has no return path; the sketch's `promote()` only changes `u.class` and goes straight to S6, contradicting row 4. `sendbacks.decompose` is not charged, so T0→T1→T2→T3 yields three uncounted re-plans.
findings.fix: Promotion never re-plans: the unit keeps its id, branch and diff. Run only the unit-scoped skipped stages: S4 post-hoc (prober writes the acceptance test that fails on base_sha; contract-checker vets), S2 in audit-only mode (auditor + coverage of the existing card vs the actual diff), then re-run gate → S6 at the new class → S7. If the audit says 'must split' → treat as row 7 (I=replan, `sendbacks.decompose++`) with the diff kept as `starting_commit` for the children. If new class ≥ T2, the script returns `{ask:'H1', unit}` and parks only that unit (siblings continue); the driver relaunches. Cap promotions at 1 per unit; a second → H3.

findings.section: §6 row 16 vs §7.4 narrative scan; §6 row 1 hash rule
findings.claim: Row 16's remedy ('add rationale: doc comment / ADR / test name') is either invisible to the blind lens and triggers row 1, or is stripped by the narrative scan's uncapped 'neutralize' loop, so ILLEGIBLE units go to H3 by construction.
findings.scenario: T1 unit, cold lens: ILLEGIBLE → row 16 → S5 'add rationale'. Case A: executor writes an ADR line in `.separator/decisions.md` → not in the code diff → `diff_sha256` unchanged → row 1 'artifact hash unchanged after a send-back' → ESCALATE H3; the sandbox strips `.separator` anyway, so the cold lens could never have read it. Case B: executor adds `// Implements A2: discount applies after tax (ruling R14)` and renames the test `test_discount_after_tax_R14` → §7.4 scan (ruling ids, plan nouns from the cards) hits → 'neutralize narrative' task (free, uncapped) → executor strips it → S7 → ILLEGIBLE again → 'second time → H3 (design problem)'. Two S5 rounds, three S7 runs and a human touch on a change that may be fine. The neutralize loop has no cap: a test name containing a legitimate domain noun that is also in the card vocabulary re-triggers every time; at T0 the extra calls trip the `calls` cap → row 1.
findings.fix: (i) Rationale must be in the tree (doc comment, test name, README paragraph); drop 'ADR' from row 16; if the DEFER-GATE round leaves the hash unchanged, return to the executor once with 'rationale must be in the diff' instead of row 1. (ii) Narrative allow-list: ACCEPTANCE.md text and its nouns are never narrative (the customer lens sees them anyway); strip only epic/unit ids, run-dir paths, ruling ids, reviewer/round vocabulary. (iii) Neutralize inside the sandbox via `redact.sh` (replace hits with `[…]` in the sandbox copy only), never by sending the executor back — zero calls, no loop; record `narrative_terms[]` as a concern. (iv) State that the DEFER-GATE round does not charge `sendbacks.execute` and is capped at 1.

findings.section: §3 S3 cross-epic locks; §8.4; §4 locks.json (gitignored); §5.1 (no queue timeout)
findings.claim: Locks are released only at merge, live in a per-checkout gitignored file, and are re-checked only at S3 entry, so killed/parked/crashed epics hold locks forever, SCOPE-REQUEST widening can deadlock two epics, and two sessions never see each other's locks.
findings.scenario: A (leak): epic E1's T2 unit U2 holds serialized resource `migrations` (acquired at S3), reaches H2, the human kills the epic → no merge → `locks.json` still lists E1. Epic E2 touching migrations queues at S3; no H3/H4 packet says 'E2 waits on E1'; E2 ends only via the 14-day lifetime → PARTIAL. Same after a crash mid-wave (no owner liveness) and after a PARTIAL verdict. B (deadlock): E1 and E2 pass S3 with disjoint sets; E1.U1 files SCOPE-REQUEST for `shared/config.ts` held by E2.V1 → row 3 → S3 → queued; E2.V1 files SCOPE-REQUEST for `api/client.ts` held by E1.U1 → queued. Both waves block at the barrier; no timeout, no detector. C: two `claude --worktree` sessions each have their own gitignored `locks.json` → both dispatch overlapping units → row 18 ping-pong → serialize + H3.
findings.fix: Locks carry `{epic, unit, acquired_at, session}` and are released on merge, kill, park-of-owner, PARTIAL and epic lifetime; `status.sh` (SessionStart) sweeps locks whose owner's state.json is not in-flight. A queued unit records `queued_since`; after `policy.lock_wait_h` (default 24) it becomes an H3 card naming the holder. Any widening (SCOPE-REQUEST, promotion, amendment) re-runs the cross-epic check with wait-for-graph cycle detection; a cycle sends the younger epic's unit to H3 immediately (never queues). Store locks at `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/separator/locks.json` under `flock` so all worktrees and sessions share one file.

findings.section: §5.3 hold; §6 row 15; §9 H2 'send back'; §5.4 counter reset; §5.2 sigs_seen
findings.claim: A blind hazard without repro can be re-raised by every fresh cold lens after each H2 send-back with no cap (blind lenses never see rulings; hold sigs are line-sensitive and never deduped), and a human H3 resolution cannot clear `sigs_seen` or the 'same repro fails again' rule, so 'retry with hint' is structurally ineffective.
findings.scenario: A: T1 unit; cold lens files hazard `concurrency/race` at `handler.go:42`, no repro; verifier cannot reproduce ('unverifiable is never refuted') → HOLD → class T2 → H2 card. Human: 'send back (default S5): add a mutex'. Executor adds it; gate; S6 delta; S7 with a FRESH cold lens that by design never sees rulings → files the same hazard class at `handler.go:44` → `sig = sha1(file:line:claim)` differs (line moved) → not in sigs_seen → verifier → unverifiable → HOLD → H2 again. Each cycle: one human touch + 4–5 calls; `human_escalations` counts only H3; nothing bounds it. B: H3 'same repro fails again'; human picks 'retry S5 with hint' → §5.4 resets only the named counter (`sendbacks.execute`); `sigs_seen[]` and the same-repro rule are not counters → next round the frozen regress test fails once more → H3 immediately → human_escalations 2 → 3 → epic parked with zero agent progress.
findings.fix: Hazard sig = sha1(hazard_class + file + normalized claim), line-insensitive. An H2 decision on a HOLD (approve or send back) writes `ruled_hazards[sig]` in state.json; decide.sh row 15 counts only UNRULED hazards, and a re-raised ruled hazard is downgraded to `concern`. A HOLD re-raised twice without a ruling → H3, not H2. §5.4: an H3 resolution is `{reset:{counters:[…], sigs:[…]}}` and the same-repro/unchanged-hash rules are suspended for exactly one round after a reset that names the sig.

findings.section: §3 S5 (guard-scope, SCOPE-REQUEST, Stop hook); §6 row 3; §12.4 hooks; §5.2 ratchet.sh runner
findings.claim: The executor's only legal exit for a too-narrow write-set (SCOPE-REQUEST.md) is denied by guard-scope and blocked by the Stop hook's forced retries, so row 3's cheap S3 branch is unreachable and every scope problem costs two executor rounds plus a replan.
findings.scenario: T1 unit, writes `[src/cart/*.ts]`; the executor finds the acceptance test needs one line in `src/pricing/tax.ts`. It must write `units/<u>/SCOPE-REQUEST.md`; guard-scope denies `.separator/**` except `units/<u>/notes.md` and denies `src/pricing/**`. SubagentStop `require-evidence.sh` runs the fast gate (acceptance test red) → exit 2, three times → `status: fail` → `exec_retries` → a fresh executor hits the same wall → S2 with gate output (`sendbacks.decompose` 1 = T1 cap) → planner widens → the next scope issue in this unit → H3. §3 S5 also says SCOPE-REQUEST 'routes to S2' while row 3 says S3 — contradictory. Likewise `ratchet.sh` must write frozen `tests/regress_*` before re-dispatch, but scripts have no filesystem access and the executor is hook-denied on that glob; no runner is named, so the ratchet as specified cannot execute.
findings.fix: Allow-list `units/<u>/SCOPE-REQUEST.md` (and notes.md) in guard-scope; `require-evidence.sh` allows an immediate stop with `status: scope-request` when that file exists (no retries, no charge to Stop-hook or exec_retries); decide.sh row 3 keys on `status == scope-request` (S=yes) → S3 re-schedule with `scope_requests++` (cap 1, then S2); make §3 S5 say S3 to match row 3. State that ratchet.sh, like gate.sh and sandbox.sh, runs as `agent('Run ratchet.sh …', sep-verifier, effort low)` and that its file writes are exempt from guard-scope because they come from bin/ scripts, not agent Write calls.

findings.section: §3 S2 exit gate ('≤12 units per epic (else split epic)', 'second failure → H3')
findings.claim: 'Split epic' is prose with no artifact or driver action, so any request needing more than 12 units dead-ends at H3 before any code is written — exactly the large-project case the workflow is for.
findings.scenario: Request 'migrate all 140 REST handlers to the new auth middleware' on the user's monolith. Planner produces 18 units of ≤8 files. S2 gate: >12 units → violation → planner re-invoked ONCE with the violation list → it merges units to 12 (now `est_files > 8`) → gate fails → 'second failure → H3'. The H3 options (pick option / ruling / kill) cannot split either; the driver has no command that creates child epics, and `sendbacks.decompose`/`human_escalations` are spent on a limitation of the harness. Every large request stalls at S2 with a human touch and zero progress.
findings.fix: Let the planner return `dag.json.split: [{suffix, request_slice, ac_ids[], depends_on_epic?}]` when the honest unit count exceeds 12; the driver creates child epics (`<epic>-1`, `<epic>-2`, …) that share ACCEPTANCE ids and run sequentially (or in parallel when their write-sets and serialized resources are disjoint per locks.json), each ≤12 units; this is not an escalation (no H3, no counter), just one line in the H4 digest. The S2 gate rejects a plan that both exceeds 12 units and lacks `split`.

findings.section: §3 S5 (Who/Hooks), §8.2, §12.1 sep-executor/sep-prober/sep-inspector `isolation: worktree`, §12.4 guard-scope 'unit from branch name'
findings.claim: `isolation: worktree` cannot give an executor a worktree on `sep/<epic>/<unit>` from `base_sha`: Claude Code branches every subagent worktree from the remote default branch (fetching origin/HEAD) or, with `worktree.baseRef: "head"`, from the main checkout's HEAD, on an auto-generated `worktree-<name>` branch, and the docs state `baseRef` cannot name a branch.
findings.scenario: Epic E, wave 2 unit U3 depends on U1 already merged to `integration` (not yet promoted to `main`). sep-executor(U3) is spawned with `isolation: worktree` → its worktree starts from `origin/main`, U1's interface does not exist → contract checks fail → gate fail → `exec_retries` → same result → S2 send-back for every wave-2 unit in every epic. Independently, `guard-scope.sh` runs `git branch --show-current` and gets `worktree-bright-fox`, so it finds no unit and must either deny all edits (executor dead) or allow all (scope guard void). On the one legal retry, attempt 2 gets a fresh worktree from main and `git checkout sep/E/U3` is refused by git because attempt 1's kept worktree still has that branch checked out.
findings.fix: Remove `isolation: worktree` from sep-executor, sep-prober and sep-inspector. Add `.separator/bin/wt.sh <epic> <unit> <base_sha>` run by a Bash-only `sep-ops` agent before each dispatch: `git worktree add -B sep/<epic>/<unit> .claude/worktrees/sep-<epic>-<unit> <base_sha>` when absent, reuse in place on retry, and commit the frozen acceptance tests as `<unit> change set 0`. Every executor/prober prompt carries `WORKTREE=<abs path>`; frontmatter PreToolUse hooks enforce `tool_input.file_path` and stdin `cwd` under `WORKTREE` and derive `<epic>/<unit>` from `git -C "$cwd" branch --show-current` (now deterministic). Inspector gets `git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/insp-<unit> sep/<epic>/<unit>`. Document that `worktree.baseRef` is irrelevant to the funnel.

findings.section: §3 S4/S5 Outputs, §4 artifact layout (`.separator/epics/` gitignored), §12.1 sep-prober 'Write limited to tests/probes', sep-executor evidence.json/notes.md
findings.claim: An `isolation: worktree` agent cannot write any ledger artifact: Claude Code blocks Edit/Write to paths in the main checkout, and `.separator/epics/` is gitignored so it does not exist inside the worktree either, which strands spike.json, the acceptance test, evidence.json and notes.md.
findings.scenario: sep-prober(U1) finishes its spike and calls `Write .separator/epics/E/units/U1/tests/acc_U1.test.ts` (main checkout path) → tool error 'targets the main checkout'. It writes the test inside its worktree instead; the `red-proof.sh` Stop hook looks in the ledger path, finds no test, exits 2 three times, the prober stops with no usable output; the workflow sees `acc_tests: []` and every T1+ unit is sent back to S2. The same happens to the executor's `evidence.json`/`notes.md` and the retry executor never receives 'what the next attempt should know'.
findings.fix: Same manual-worktree design as impl-worktree-base-branch (no `isolation` flag, so main-checkout writes are legal) plus explicit ownership: the prober writes the acceptance test into the worktree tree at the zone's test path and `wt.sh` commits it as change set 0 on the unit branch; spike/evidence/notes are returned through the agent's `schema` and persisted by `sep-ops` (`bin/ledger.sh put <epic> <unit> <file> <<json`); the executor's frontmatter guard-scope allow-list is `${WORKTREE}/**` ∩ `writes[]` plus `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.separator/epics/<epic>/units/<unit>/{notes.md,evidence.json}`.

findings.section: §7.3 Launch, §12.4 rows 'agent: sep-outsider-*', 'agent: sep-executor SubagentStop', 'agent: sep-prober SubagentStop'
findings.claim: Agent frontmatter accepts only `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse` and `Stop` hooks (Stop is auto-converted to SubagentStop at runtime; SubagentStart/SubagentStop are settings.json-only), and SubagentStart can never block (exit code ignored, stderr shown to the user), so `assert-sandbox.sh` is unimplementable as written and every frontmatter `SubagentStop` entry is an invalid event name.
findings.scenario: sep-outsider-cold is defined with `hooks: {SubagentStart: assert-sandbox.sh, SubagentStop: check-evidence.sh + leak-scan.sh}`. Neither event is honoured in frontmatter; the agent spawns with cwd = project root, no sandbox check and no evidence enforcement. Its first call is `Read /proj/src/cart.ts` (live tree, not the sandbox). `guard-blind.sh` has no way to know which unit's sandbox this agent belongs to (hooks never see the prompt; two units are in S7 concurrently), so it either denies everything (lens dead) or lets the judge read the live tree with `.claude/`, plan vocabulary and other units' code. Likewise the executor's `SubagentStop: require-evidence.sh` never runs, so 'evidence not claims' is unenforced.
findings.fix: (1) Rename every frontmatter `SubagentStop` to `Stop`; delete frontmatter `SubagentStart`; if a spawn log is wanted, register `SubagentStart` in settings.json with `matcher: "^sep-outsider-"` as a logger only. (2) `guard-blind.sh` (frontmatter PreToolUse `Read|Grep|Glob|Bash`) uses a static allow-list instead of a per-agent path: allow only paths under `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.separator/epics/*/blind/*/{sandbox,pack}/` whose sibling `manifest.json` validates; allow Bash only when stdin `cwd` is inside such a sandbox or the command is exactly `cd <that sandbox>`; deny `git -C`, `--git-dir`, `GIT_DIR=`, `..`, any other absolute path, and network tools; append `agent_id<TAB>path` to `<sandbox>/reads.log`. (3) `leak-scan.sh` at `Stop` asserts all `reads.log` lines for this `agent_id` fall under one sandbox; `check-evidence.sh` parses `last_assistant_message` for non-empty `evidence[]` and exits 2 once, honouring `stop_hook_active`. (4) Optionally build sandboxes outside the repo (`~/.cache/separator/<epic>/<unit>`) so the cross-family `claude -p` lens cannot walk up to the project's CLAUDE.md/settings.

findings.section: §3 S5 Hooks, §12.1 sep-executor `permissionMode: acceptEdits`, §12.4 selftest ('bypassPermissions not set'), §9 'everything else is unattended'
findings.claim: Nothing in the spec prevents a permission prompt on every distinct Bash command an executor, prober, judge or ops agent runs, and a workflow run pauses on each such prompt, so an 'unattended' wave becomes a stream of human approvals and the human is back IN the loop.
findings.scenario: T1 epic, wave of 4 executors in `acceptEdits` (which only covers file edits). Each runs `pnpm test -- discount`, `git add -A`, `git commit -m "U2 change set 1"`, `.separator/bin/gate.sh E U2`; in default/manual mode each new command shape prompts the user; the run pauses at the first prompt; with the human away for the weekend nothing auto-merges to `integration`, and §10's 'touches 3 → 0.3' is false in practice. `selftest.sh` forbids `bypassPermissions`, the only setting that would have avoided it.
findings.fix: Make `guard-bash.sh` the single decider using the documented `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision`: `allow` for `.separator/bin/*`, `git (add|commit|diff|status|log|rev-parse|show|worktree list) *`, every literal in `zones.json.commands.*` and `contract.json.checks[].cmd`, and `cd $WORKTREE`; `deny` for the deny-list; `ask` for the rest. `guard-scope.sh` likewise returns `allow` for in-write-set edits. `/sep init` also emits `permissions.allow` (`Bash(.separator/bin/*)`, `Workflow(sep-intake)`, `Workflow(sep-plan)`, `Workflow(sep-build)`, `Workflow(sep-learn)`, `Workflow(sep-fast)`), and `selftest.sh` runs a fixture executor and asserts zero PermissionRequest events fired; keep `bypassPermissions` forbidden.

findings.section: §7.3, §7.5 'May not: git history, branch names, commit messages', §12.1 sep-outsider-* (`omitClaudeMd`)
findings.claim: `omitClaudeMd: true` does not stop Claude Code from injecting a git status snapshot (current branch, main branch, `git status`, recent commits) and the project skill roster into every subagent's system prompt, so blind lenses receive epic/unit identifiers before their first tool call and the canary never sees it.
findings.scenario: The main checkout sits on `integration`; its last commits are `Merge sep/0926-cart-discount/U1` with trailer `Separator-Epic: 0926-cart-discount` (as §3 S8 prescribes). sep-outsider-cold starts; its system prompt lists those commits; its `knowledge_statement` says 'this appears to be part of a cart-discount epic already under review'. The canary token lives only in dag.json/cards so there is no hit, `reads.log` is empty, `leak-check.json` is clean, the verdict counts — blindness is broken silently and the 'everyone agreed on the wrong thing' catch is gone.
findings.fix: `/sep init` writes `"includeGitInstructions": false` into `.claude/settings.json` and `selftest.sh` fails if it is unset; outsiders and verifiers get `disallowedTools: Skill, Agent, WebFetch, WebSearch, SendMessage, TodoWrite`; extend the narrative scan to `knowledge_statement` for the epic id, unit ids and the `sep/` prefix; keep integration merge commit subjects neutral (`integrate <sha8>`, trailers only); selftest plants a fixture commit with a trailer and asserts the cold lens's `knowledge_statement` does not contain it.

findings.section: §12.4 rows PreToolUse Edit|Write guard-scope and Bash guard-bash, §5.1 'counters incremented by scripts', §12.2 '/sep writes returned JSON to the run dir'
findings.claim: The global Edit|Write and Bash guards as tabled deny the harness's own writers (driver skill, planner, learner, integrator, sandbox.sh, wt.sh), and `state.json` has no legal writer at all because workflow scripts have no filesystem access and every agent is hook-denied.
findings.scenario: `sep-build.js` returns `{merged, parked}`; `/sep` in the main session calls `Write .separator/epics/E/state.json` → guard-scope denies it as a gate file, so counters are never persisted and the next boundary replays round 0. `sep-integrator` runs `git merge --no-ff sep/E/U1` on `integration` → guard-bash denies 'merge to integration without MERGE_APPROVED' (T1 has none, and the hook is not told which decision.json applies). `sep-ops` runs `sandbox.sh`, whose `git init -b main` matches the 'main' deny pattern → no sandbox → row 5 fires twice → INVALID → H3 on every unit.
findings.fix: Route every ledger mutation through `.separator/bin/*.sh` invoked via Bash (`state.sh apply <<json`, `ledger.sh put`, `ratchet.sh`, `land.sh`), so the Edit|Write guard is never involved; keep one thin global Edit|Write hook that protects only `request.md ACCEPTANCE.md gate.json decision.json state.json MANIFEST.json`; move role-specific guards into frontmatter (scoped by construction) and, where a settings.json hook must be role-aware, read the documented `agent_type` stdin field inside the script (PreToolUse matchers match tool names, not agent types); `land.sh <epic> <unit>` is the only merge path and itself verifies `decision.json.diff_sha256` or `MERGE_APPROVED` before `git merge`; the `/sep` driver persists workflow output with `bin/state.sh apply`.

findings.section: §12.2 sep-build.js sketch, §6 inputs L and M, §5.2 ratchet
findings.claim: The sketch relies on data no agent returns (`L` from leak-check.json, `M` from a judge that is only called on a split), on a filesystem effect the script cannot perform (`ratchet()` writing `tests/regress_<sig>`), and a throwing pipeline stage silently erases the unit from both `merged` and `parked`.
findings.scenario: U2's blind lens output fails the BLIND schema five times (verbose findings) → `agent()` throws inside the pipeline stage → U2's result is `null` → `results.filter(Boolean)` drops it → `blocked` omits U2's descendants → wave 2's U4 executes on a base without U2, gate fails, `exec_retries`, S2 send-back: three wasted calls and U2 never appears on any card or in state. Meanwhile `decide()` sees `L === undefined` so row 5 (leak) is dead code, `M` is never computed so row 16 never fires, `ratchet()` returns cards without any regress test existing, and `merged.filter(m => !m.done)` re-integrates wave-1 units on every later wave.
findings.fix: Wrap each pipeline stage body in try/catch returning `{u, stuck:'harness', why:String(e)}`; compute `blocked` as `wave` minus units with `merge:true`; set `r.done = true` after integration. Add explicit round-trips: after the blind fan-out `const post = await agent('run .separator/bin/postblind.sh E U (leak-scan + intent MATCH/MISMATCH); return JSON', {agentType:'sep-judge', effort:'low', schema:POST})` yielding `{L, M}`; `cards = await agent('run .separator/bin/ratchet.sh E U <<cards', {agentType:'sep-ops', schema:RATCHET})`; persist evidence/gate/inspect/blind JSON from script variables via `sep-ops` (`bin/ledger.sh put`). Also add `label`/`phase` to every call inside pipeline stages (phase() state races inside pipeline).

findings.section: §9 Rules ('notifications go through the Notification hook'), §12.4 row Notification `*` notify.sh
findings.claim: The `Notification` hook fires only for Claude Code's own notification types (permission_prompt, idle_prompt, agent_completed, quota_*, elicitation_*), never for a merge card, stuck card or question packet becoming ready, so `policy.notify` never receives a packet.
findings.scenario: A T2 unit reaches H2 at 18:00; `notify.sh` is registered under `Notification` with matcher `*`; the workflow ends cleanly, no permission or idle event occurs, nothing is sent; the owner returns after three days, `gate_timeout_h` (72) has parked the epic, and the promised 'T0/T1 keep flowing while T2 waits' turns into 'everything waited for a notification that cannot exist'.
findings.fix: Emit packet notifications from the driver: `/sep` runs `bin/notify.sh` after each workflow returns and whenever `status.sh --pending` lists a packet; add a main-session `Stop` hook (`status.sh --pending && notify.sh`) so a packet is announced when Claude finishes the turn; keep `Notification` only with matcher `permission_prompt|idle_prompt` to alert 'run paused'; state in §9 that away-notification needs a terminal-independent channel (webhook or file watched by the user).

findings.section: §12.1 agents table (sep-cartographer, sep-contract-checker, sep-inspector, model column)
findings.claim: Several frontmatter values in §12.1 are not valid Claude Code syntax or conflict with each other.
findings.scenario: `sep-cartographer` declares `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash(git log, ls-files)`: the parenthesised text is one specifier `git log, ls-files` that matches no command, so the cartographer has no working Bash and cannot read churn; `sep-contract-checker`'s `Bash(read-only)` is not a specifier; `sep-inspector`'s `memory: project` auto-enables Read/Write/Edit (contradicting its read-only role) and its memory dir `.claude/agent-memory/` would be in the main checkout; `model: haiku-class / small / strong` are not recognised aliases.
findings.fix: Use `Bash(git log *)`, `Bash(git ls-files *)`, `Bash(git blame *)`; for the checker enumerate read-only commands (`Bash(grep *)`, `Bash(rg *)`, `Bash(ls *)`, `Bash(cat *)`, plus the zone build/test literals) or give it no Bash and let it request probes via `sep-ops`; drop `memory` on inspector and cartographer (principle 1: lessons.md and zones.json are the memory); write `model: haiku`, `sonnet`, `inherit`; note that `permissionMode` in frontmatter is ignored when the main session runs in `auto`, `acceptEdits` or `bypassPermissions`.

findings.section: §12.2 driver/`sep-fast.js`, §11 'tokens from the workflow budget API', §12.2 'resumable by runId'
findings.claim: Two secondary assumptions about the workflow runtime do not hold: per-unit token cost is not obtainable from `budget`, and each saved workflow prompts for launch approval on every run in manual/acceptEdits mode unless approved with 'don't ask again' per script per project or listed in `permissions.allow`.
findings.scenario: `/sep` launches `sep-build`; the user sees 'Yes / Yes and don't ask again / View script / No' — at least once for each of the five scripts, and on every run if they pick plain Yes. §11 computes 'tokens per unit' from `budget.spent()`, which is a turn-wide shared output-token pool across all concurrent agents (`budget.total` is null unless the user typed a '+Nk' directive), so U1 vs U2 attribution is impossible and calls-per-unit metrics silently read the wrong number.
findings.fix: `/sep init` adds `Workflow(sep-intake|sep-plan|sep-build|sep-learn|sep-fast)` allow rules and tells the user to pick 'don't ask again' once per script; take per-agent tokens post-hoc from the run's `journal.jsonl` / `/workflows` view via `bin/metrics.sh ingest <runId>` (a driver step) instead of the budget API; `sep-fast.js` may call `workflow('sep-intake', args)` etc. (one level only, so those children must not call `workflow()` themselves); persist each boundary's `runId` in `state.json` and document that `resumeFromRunId` works only within the same session, otherwise the driver starts a new run with the same `args` (idempotent via `inputs_sha`).

findings.section: §3 S1b, §3 S4 exit gate + skip rule, §6 row 22, §2.1 modifiers, §11 shadow defaults
findings.claim: On a repo without a test framework (the target vibe-coder's typical state) the first task in any zone either dead-ends at H3 or is permanently forced into a human merge card, so the fast lane never exists there.
findings.scenario: Next.js app, zones.json inferred: test:null, build:"next build", lint:"eslint .". Request "make the header background blue" (1 file, T0 by size). S1: commands.test == null → S1b prober (1 call, ≤15 turns) tries to write characterization tests; no runner installed and installing one is outside its write-set → "no runnable check can be produced" → verification degrades to observation AND class is raised to T1. Zone is only `inferred` (Hz confirmation is batched into the daily H4), so the S4 skip rule (T1 with unknowns==[] and zone declared) does not apply → S4 runs → its exit gate demands an acceptance test that FAILS on base_sha for the right reason → impossible for an observation unit → verdict replan → S2 → planner cannot change the facts → second failure → H3 stuck card. Best case (prober manages a snapshot test): the unit is observation-only → §6 row 22 HOLD → merge card on every UI task forever; `/sep init` shadow mode ("everything T1") makes every first-week task take this path.
findings.fix: (1) Treat build/lint/typecheck as `check` commands: S1b fires only when build, lint, test and smoke are ALL null. (2) S4 for units whose contract checks are `observation`: deliverable = observation recipe (run/smoke command + what to look at) plus any smoke `check` that exists; no RED-on-base requirement; red-proof.sh is skipped for observation contracts. (3) Row 22: T0/T1 observation units auto-merge when the customer lens executed run/smoke with non-empty evidence, Bc=PASS and H=0; HOLD only at T2+. (4) Drop the automatic class +1 for observation at T0/T1 (keep at T2+). (5) Fold S1b into the unit's own S4 prober call (scaffold + acceptance test in one call, `test_writes` granted for the zone's tests/**); a separate bootstrap branch only when ≥2 units of the wave share the zone.

findings.section: §3 S0 (intent-checker, comparator), §12.2 sep-build.js sketch, §6 input M, §5.1 `calls` cap, §10 T0 row
findings.claim: A single T0 request costs 7–9 subagent invocations, not 2.2: the intent-checker and comparator are never skipped, every deterministic script (gate.sh, sandbox.sh, integrate) is executed through a `sep-verifier` agent call because scripts have no filesystem access, and the M intent-match needs a `sep-judge` call; a typo fix becomes 10–25 min wall-clock and the T0 `calls ≤ 4` cap trips if runner calls are counted.
findings.scenario: Solo dev types `/sep fix typo "recieve" in README.md`. sep-intake.js: parallel([triage, intent-checker]) = 2 calls (single request → triage is 1.0, not the amortized 0.2); the two AC lists differ in wording → comparator = call 3. sep-fast.js: executor (4), `Run gate.sh` via sep-verifier (5), `Run sandbox.sh` via sep-verifier (6), cold lens (7), sep-judge for M (8), sep-integrator (9). At harness concurrency 2 that is ≥7 serial call latencies of 1–3 min each. If `state.units.u.calls` counts subagent invocations as §10 defines them, 9 > cap 4 → §6 row 1 ESCALATE → H3 stuck card for a typo; if only executor calls count (as in the sketch's `st.calls++`), the §11 target "T0 ≤ 3 calls" is unattainable and §10's "worst case is a straight line plus one cheap insurance call" is false. Straight-line chat: one edit, ~1 minute.
findings.fix: (a) S0 rule: intent-checker and comparator are skipped when class==T0 and unknowns==[] (the T0 cold-lens back-translation §7.6 already supplies the second opinion on intent). (b) Run deterministic scripts from hooks, which do have filesystem access: `require-evidence.sh` (executor SubagentStop) runs the full `gate.sh` and the executor's structured output carries gate.json path+sha (gate.json stays script-written); `assert-sandbox.sh` (outsider SubagentStart) builds the sandbox when no manifest exists for (base_sha, head_sha); decide/ratchet stay pure code in the script; one `sep-integrator` call per wave. Target T0 = 2 LLM calls, 0 runner calls. (c) Run the M judgement only at T1+ or when the cold lens returned ILLEGIBLE; T0 with cold SAFE + gate green merges. (d) Define `calls` in §5.1/§10 as stage-agent invocations only; runner/verifier calls are excluded from caps and reported separately in metrics.

findings.section: §8.4 WIP limit, §10 mechanism (3) parallelism, §12.2 parallel()/pipeline()
findings.claim: The parallelism argument ("8 independent T1 units ≈ 1–2 chain lengths") assumes ≥8 concurrent agents; with the reference harness cap of 2 the per-unit critical path is 7–11 serial call latencies and a multi-unit epic is slower than doing the tasks one by one in chat.
findings.scenario: T2 epic, 4 independent units in one wave, harness concurrency 2. Per unit: 2 spikes + contract-checker (2 slots), executor (1), gate runner (1), 2 inspectors (1), sandbox runner (1), 3 blind lenses (2), judge/M (1), verifier on any hold (1), integrator (1) ≈ 11 slots × 1–3 min = 11–33 min with zero send-backs. Four units share the two slots → 22–66 min of agent time before the first send-back round; §10's straight line for the same 4 tasks is 4 × 2.5 calls ≈ 10–30 min. The `pipeline(wave)` with nested `parallel(lenses)` also lets lenses of unit A starve the executor of unit B, lengthening the critical path further. §10 models none of this.
findings.fix: Add `concurrency` to policy.json and to the §10 model: wall-clock = Σ_stage ceil(fanout/c)·latency along the critical path. At c ≤ 2: T1 runs ONE fresh reviewer (S6 inspector) plus ONE blind lens (customer if run≠null, else cold); both S6 and S7 only when class ≥ T2 or the zone has an escape in its 30-unit window (this is the spec's own tuning floor "T1 customer"). Build the S7 sandboxes of a wave in one batch. Schedule writers (executors, probers) ahead of read-only fan-outs in the pipeline so lenses never block the next executor. Publish the resulting critical-path table per class at c = 2 and c = 5.

findings.section: §3 S5 mechanical gate, §3 S6 "re-runs the gate itself", §8.8 suite latency budget, §5.2 ratchet, §3 S1b 3× rule
findings.claim: The full suite runs 3–5 times per unit per round (gate `full`, inspector re-run, integration `full`, 3 mutants, flake ×2, ratchet 2+3, bootstrap 3×), and §8.8 reacts to a slow suite by raising the class, which adds more suite-running stages — a perverse incentive.
findings.scenario: Django monolith, zone `full` = 12 min, T1 unit with one send-back. Round 1: gate 12 min + inspector re-run 12 + 3 mutants × 12 = 36 + integration 12; send-back: ratchet repro run 2× on branch and 3× on fix (each needs DB fixtures, ~1 min) ≈ 5; round 2 repeats gate/inspector/integration = 36 → ≈ 1h50 of suite time for one normal task. suite_seconds > 600 → the zone must declare `fast` or the class is raised to T2 → now two inspectors each re-run the gate → +24 min. The dev sees a 2-hour turnaround on a 40-line change and goes back to chat.
findings.fix: (a) gate.json is script-only, so S6 re-runs only the unit's contract checks (+ the gate's failing subset), never `full`. (b) Per-unit gate = `fast` + impacted subset via a `commands.subset` template (runner's changed/related filter, or `test_globs` mapped from changed files); `full` runs once per wave at integration only (already specified) — delete the "class is raised by one" clause of §8.8. (c) Mutants and flake re-runs execute only the contract checks. (d) Repetition uses a `commands.repeat` template (`go test -count=3`, `pytest --count`, `--repeat`) where available; otherwise run once when suite_seconds > 60 and record `flake_checked:false` instead of paying 5 suite runs.

findings.section: §7.2 sandbox construction, §7.6 customer lens runs the product, §12.2 sandbox via sep-verifier Bash
findings.claim: The blind sandbox is a `git archive` of the whole tree with no dependencies or build cache, so on a large repo every T1+ unit-round pays a full install + build (minutes to tens of minutes) inside an agent's Bash call before the customer lens can execute anything, and it is rebuilt on every send-back.
findings.scenario: pnpm monorepo, 1.2 GB tree, 40 workspace packages. sandbox.sh run by sep-verifier through Bash: `git archive` ×2 ≈ 2 min, `pnpm install` ≈ 4 min, `next build` ≈ 5 min → exceeds the Bash tool's 10-min ceiling → sandbox incomplete → customer lens reports UNVERIFIABLE → §6 row 13 SENDBACK to S0 → an H0 question for a routine T1 unit. Even when it fits, a T1 unit with one send-back pays two cold builds (~20 min) for the lens alone; §10 counts the blind stage as 1 call.
findings.fix: (a) One base sandbox per (epic, base_sha) built once from the outsider's SubagentStart hook with a timeout sized by suite_seconds; gitignored dependency/build dirs (node_modules, .venv, target, vendor) are hard-linked or `cp --reflink`ed from the executor worktree after the strip list is applied to them; each unit/round layers only the second commit on a `cp -al` copy, and the manifest records the copied dirs so blindness stays auditable. (b) Customer lens at T1 runs zone `smoke` (seconds) rather than `run` + full build; full `run` at T2+. (c) Monorepos: archive only the impact set's workspace packages plus their dependency closure, recorded as `sandbox_scope` in manifest.json.

findings.section: §3 S8 merge, §9 H4, §12.4 guard-bash.sh, §2.1 bypass lane
findings.claim: For a solo developer the integration→main split plus a daily H4 digest turns every T0/T1 into either a hidden human touch or a 24-hour delay, and the push guard forces even an emergency hotfix through the full funnel.
findings.scenario: Solo dev deploys from `main` (Vercel). 10:00 typo fix through /sep lands on `integration`; nothing deploys until they run `/sep promote` (a touch §10 counts as 0 for T0/T1) or tomorrow's digest. 02:00, prod is down: they edit 4 files on main; `git push` is denied by guard-bash (no decision.json for a T0/T1 diff); `/sep check` classifies the diff T1 (4 files) → "promoted into the funnel as a unit" → spike, executor, gate, inspector, sandbox, 2 lenses, judge → 20–40 min while prod is down. They disable the hooks in settings.json and never re-enable them.
findings.fix: `policy.promotion ∈ {digest, auto_t01, per_epic}`; `/sep init` selects `auto_t01` when `git shortlog -sn` shows a single author: T0/T1 units with zero `intent` assumptions and H=0 merge straight to main (or integration==main), and the H4 digest becomes a post-hoc review with one-click revert. Guards are no-ops unless the current branch matches `sep/<epic>/<unit>` (unit-from-branch is already the design). `/sep check` on a human diff never blocks a push: it runs gate + S6/S7 post-hoc in the background and files findings as tickets or escape lines; the bypass is counted in metrics so the ratchet still raises the zone floor if escapes follow.

findings.section: §11 shadow mode paragraph, §13 day-one adoption
findings.claim: Shadow mode makes the user do every task twice for the first 10 runs (full funnel at "everything T1" plus their own straight-line work) and the baseline it collects is contaminated, so the adoption path is the most expensive and abandonment-prone part of the design.
findings.scenario: Day one, solo dev, 10 small tasks. Each shadow run costs ~10 calls in the T1 lane (spike, executor, gate, inspector, sandbox, 2 lenses, judge) ≈ 20–60 min of agent time and produces a merge card that is thrown away; the dev then implements the task by hand after reading the funnel's findings, so the "straight-line" baseline is measured on a human who already knows the answer. By task 4 they stop typing /sep; the ledger never reaches 10 runs and the priors are never replaced.
findings.fix: Shadow = bypass lane: the human works as before; a pre-push hook or `/sep check` runs gate + ONE cold lens on each human commit (≤2 calls, background) and logs findings → that is the finding/escape baseline. The straight-line time baseline is computed from git history (median inter-commit time and fix/hotfix commit ratio per zone over the last 30 days) with no duplicate work. Enable the T0 lane immediately (it is cheap once finding #2 is applied) and switch T1+ on per zone after 10 bypass checks; require 30 units, not 10, before priors are replaced.

findings.section: §3 S5 mechanical gate (mutant probes) vs §2.1 class table Gate column, §6 row 10, §3 S5 hooks (frozen test_globs)
findings.claim: §3 runs mutant probes on every code change while §2.1 lists them only at T2; at T0/T1 they cost three extra suite runs and turn untested-but-correct lines (logging, CSS, copy, config) into unfixable E6 send-backs because the executor cannot add tests outside its write-set.
findings.scenario: T1 unit: change a log format string and one condition; the contract test covers the condition. Canned mutation "return constant" on the log line survives → E6 finding with built-in repro → §6 row 10 SENDBACK S5; frozen `test_globs` deny the executor a new test; round 2 the same mutant survives → "same repro fails again" → H3 stuck card for a log line. Each mutant ran zone `full` (5 min) → +15 min per unit even when everything is killed.
findings.fix: Align §3 with §2.1: mutants at T2+ only. Apply mutations only to changed lines in files the unit's contract checks exercise (coverage report if available, else the acceptance test's target files); run only the contract checks per mutant, not `full`; a surviving mutant is an `important` finding at T2+ and a `note` below. Every card grants `test_writes` for `units/<u>/tests/**` and `tests/regress_*` so an executor can kill a mutant by adding a test.

findings.section: §10 table and "why net faster" paragraph
findings.claim: The §10 table's h=2 and h=10 columns do not follow from its own formula, touches are counted asymmetrically (straight line charged 2 touches for a typo, funnel 0 although the request must still be typed and the digest read/acked), and the call counts contradict the §12.2 sketch, so the acceleration claim is unsupported for exactly the solo-dev case (h→0) the spec admits it loses.
findings.scenario: The only L(h) that reproduces the T0-funnel column is L = 6 + 3h. Applying it: T0 straight h=2 = 1 + 4 + 0.10·12 = 6.2 (table 7.2), h=10 = 24.6 (table 23.6); T1 straight 11.6 / 42.8 (table 12.6 / 41.8); T1 funnel 6.5 / 10.1 (table 6.8 / 9.7); T2 straight (L = 20 + 8h) 21.3 / 72.5 (table 22.7 / 71.1); T2 funnel 14.1 / 24.0 (table 15.0 / 23.0). At a solo dev's h ≈ 0.5: T1 straight = 2 + 1.5 + 0.30·7.5 = 5.75; T1 funnel = 5.8 with the table's 5.3 calls and ≈ 10.5 with the sketch's real ~10 calls (each send-back round re-runs gate, inspector, sandbox, lenses and judge, not the 0.9 "rounds" allowance) → the funnel is ~2× slower on T1 unless c≥5 parallelism or escape savings rescue it. Token cost at T0 is ~8× a chat by the sketch, not "2–4×". e_s = 0.10 for a straight-line typo and e_f = 0.03 for a single low-effort cold lens with no test coverage are asserted, not derived.
findings.fix: Republish the table with: (i) L(h) stated once and applied consistently; (ii) symmetric touches — both paths pay the request touch, the funnel pays its digest/ack share; (iii) call counts taken from the sketch per class, split into LLM calls and runner calls, including expected send-back rounds at p = 0.45; (iv) wall-clock = serial-path latencies at `policy.concurrency`; (v) a break-even line per class: the straight-line escape rate at which funnel = straight for h ∈ {0.5, 2, 6}; put the solo-dev column first. Keep error-prevention by letting the model justify each lens per class rather than assuming it.

findings.section: §3 S5 hooks (PostToolUse Edit|Write → zone fast lint), §12.4 lint-file.sh
findings.claim: The PostToolUse Edit|Write hook runs the zone `fast` lint after every single edit; in ecosystems where the cheapest lint is a compile (Rust, Go, project-wide tsc, JVM) that is 10–90 s × 20–40 edits per executor run, multiplying executor wall-clock 3–10× and burning the Stop-hook budget.
findings.scenario: Rust crate, zone fast = "cargo clippy -p crate" (incremental ≈ 25 s). The executor makes 30 edits → 12.5 min of hook time inside a T1 budget; each hook returns stderr noise into the transcript, consuming maxTurns; `require-evidence.sh` then runs `fast` again at SubagentStop; the unit hits the Stop cap, exits `status: fail`, gets one fresh retry (same cost) and is sent to S2 — for a change that was fine.
findings.fix: The cartographer records `fast_seconds` and whether a file-scoped lint exists; `lint-file.sh` runs only when `fast_seconds ≤ 5` and a file-scoped command is declared (`eslint <file>`, `ruff <file>`, `gofmt -l <file>`), otherwise it is a no-op and `fast` runs once in `require-evidence.sh`; hook `timeout` is set from `fast_seconds`; PostToolUse output is truncated to the first 20 lines of diagnostics for the touched file only.

findings.section: §7.3 Launch; §12.1 sep-outsider-*; §12.2 sep-build.js sketch; §12.4 agent-scoped hooks
findings.claim: The primary L3 blind launch (workflow `agent(..., {agentType:'sep-outsider-<lens>'})` + frontmatter hooks assert-sandbox/guard-blind/leak-scan) rests on two mechanics that are empirically false in this environment: a subagent's cwd is the main checkout (probe hook.log: `agent_type=sep-probe-test cwd=/home/user/---`; docs sub-agents.md:275 'A subagent starts in the main conversation's current working directory'), and agent-frontmatter `hooks:` never fire (mechanics §9.3). So blindness is prompt-only, exactly what §7.1 says is not blindness.
findings.scenario: sep-build.js reaches S7 for unit U2 of epic 0926-cart-discount. `agent(blindPrompt(u,'cold'), {agentType:'sep-outsider-cold'})` starts in /home/user/--- with tools Read/Grep/Glob/Bash. assert-sandbox.sh and guard-blind.sh do not run (frontmatter hooks are dead), or, if moved to global settings.json, assert-sandbox refuses every launch because cwd is never a sandbox. The lens, having no commands.json, runs `Grep pattern="discount"` with no `path` (default = cwd) and gets `.separator/epics/0926-cart-discount/units/U2/card.md:Goal: apply percentage code at checkout ... Ruling R14` and `units/U2/inspect-r1.json` back; `git branch --show-current`/`git log` show `sep/0926-cart-discount/U2` and `U2 change set 2`. knowledge_statement never quotes the canary, reads.log is empty because the hook never ran → leak-check `clean` → verdict counted.
findings.fix: Make the headless launcher the PRIMARY L3 path (it is what mechanics §9.5–9.6 verified): `bin/blind.sh <sandbox> <lens>` runs, from inside the sandbox dir, `claude -p --restricted --tools Read,Grep,Glob,Bash --allowedTools Bash,Read,Grep,Glob --agents <generated-from-.claude/agents/sep-outsider-<lens>.md> --agent sep-outsider-<lens> --settings <blind-settings.json> --output-format json --json-schema <blind.schema.json> "$(cat prompts/blind-<lens>.txt)"`; the workflow calls it via a plain Bash step / `sep-verifier`, never via `agentType: sep-outsider-*`. All blind hooks (PreToolUse Bash guard, PostToolUse reads.log append, Stop check-evidence) live in blind-settings.json, not frontmatter. `--restricted` confines Read/Grep/Glob to cwd (verified: a Read of a project file was DENIED). manifest.launcher records the exact command line and CLI version. selftest.sh asserts: Read of `<project>/CLAUDE.md` DENIED, `cat ../manifest.json` DENIED, Grep without `path` cannot leave the sandbox. Delete assert-sandbox.sh (cwd is guaranteed by the launcher) and rewrite §15's 'agent-scoped frontmatter hooks' resolution.

findings.section: §4 artifact tree (`epics/<epic>/blind/<u>/sandbox`); §7.2 steps 1–6; §12.6
findings.claim: The sandbox is built INSIDE the project tree, so a headless `claude -p` launched from it auto-discovers the project CLAUDE.md hierarchy (root→cwd), which imports `@.separator/lessons.md` and pulls `.claude/rules/zone-*.md` (ruling- and defect-derived lines) into the blind context with zero tool calls; `--bare` would stop discovery but is unusable with OAuth (requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, mechanics §9.5), and the sandbox path itself (`.separator/epics/0926-cart-discount/blind/U2/sandbox`) tells the reviewer the epic's intent slug, the unit id, and that a funnel exists.
findings.scenario: lessons.md contains '- L7 (billing): percentage discounts must apply after tax (escape 2026-08)'; `.claude/rules/zone-billing.md` contains 'R14: discount applies after tax'. sandbox.sh builds `/home/user/---/.separator/epics/0926-cart-discount/blind/U2/sandbox` and blind.sh runs `claude -p` there. CLAUDE.md discovery walks up to /home/user/---/CLAUDE.md → lessons.md and zone rules are injected. The cold lens 'independently' judges the after-tax behaviour correct because it was told so; `pwd` in its first Bash call prints the epic slug; knowledge_statement says 'nothing' (no canary quoted), reads.log shows only in-sandbox reads → leak-check clean. The 'context-free' verdict was primed by the exact prior knowledge S7 exists to exclude. Additionally, the Bash guard rule 'deny any command containing the project path' (mechanics §9.5) would deny the lens's own absolute-path commands inside an in-tree sandbox.
findings.fix: `sandbox.sh` builds at `$SEP_BLIND_ROOT` (default `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/sep-blind/<sha256(tree_hash||canary_id)[:12]>/{sandbox,pack}`), outside every git repository and with an opaque directory name; only `manifest.json`, `reads.log`, `leak-check.json`, `blind-<lens>.json` stay under `epics/<epic>/blind/<u>/` (they are written by scripts, never read by the lens). Epic ids are opaque (`E-<6hex>`); the human-readable title lives only in request.md/cards/merge card. Verify in selftest.sh by planting distinct canaries in CLAUDE.md, `.claude/rules/zone-x.md`, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `lessons.md`, and `AGENTS.md`, running a cold lens, and asserting none appears in the transcript/result and `has_claude_md=false`. Update §4/§12.6: sandboxes are never under `.separator/`.

findings.section: §3 S4 outputs (`tests/acc_<u>.*`); §5.2 ratchet (`tests/regress_<sig>`); §7.4 provenance rule; §3 S5 guard-scope
findings.claim: By design every round ≥2 sandbox contains a file named `tests/regress_<sig>` whose body is the inspector's repro, and every unit's diff contains `tests/acc_<unit-id>.*` written by the prober from the card — the file names and contents reveal the unit id (decomposition), that a reviewer already found a defect (prior verdict, round count) and plan vocabulary; and the only remedy the spec offers ('neutralize narrative' task to the executor) cannot run because the executor is hook-denied from touching frozen tests.
findings.scenario: Round 1: inspector finds 'empty cart → 500', sig 4f2a; ratchet.sh commits `tests/regress_4f2a.test.ts` with `it('empty cart must not 500 (found in review)')`. Round 2 sandbox diff: `tests/acc_U2.test.ts` (+ `describe('U2: apply percentage code per card')`), `tests/regress_4f2a.test.ts`, `src/cart.ts`. The cold lens writes 'this change fixes a crash a previous reviewer reported and is the second unit of a larger feature' — refinement-aware and bandwagon bias §7.4 explicitly forbids. leak-scan flags `U2` and `regress_` as narrative_terms → executor gets 'neutralize narrative' → guard-scope denies Edit on `tests/acc_*`/`tests/regress_*` → executor stops `blocked` → gate fail → exec_retries → S2 with a bogus decompose send-back on a correct unit.
findings.fix: Naming rule enforced by red-proof.sh and ratchet.sh: test files and describe/it strings are behaviour-derived, never id-derived — `tests/<zone-convention>/<ac-slug>.test.*` for acceptance tests (slug from the AC text, e.g. `checkout_percentage_code`) and `tests/<zone>/<behaviour-slug>.test.*` for regressions (`empty_cart_total_unchanged`); the sig↔file, unit↔file mapping lives in `units/<u>/contract.json.checks[].evidence_file` and the ledger, not in the name. Prober prompt: 'test names and strings describe observable behaviour; never mention cards, rulings, rounds, reviewers or unit ids'. leak-scan's narrative list includes `acc_`, `regress_`, unit ids, sig prefixes, 'review', 'round', 'ruling', 'R<n>'. A narrative hit inside a frozen test is fixed by `ratchet.sh rename` (git mv + ledger update, 0 calls, no round charged), never routed to the executor.

findings.section: §7.6 back-translation; §6 rows 11–13 and 16; §7.2.6 pack (whole ACCEPTANCE.md per unit)
findings.claim: A correct change yields MISMATCH or a customer FAIL whenever the unit is not the whole epic: the cold lens infers the intent of ONE unit while the judge compares it with the EPIC's ACCEPTANCE.md, and the customer lens tests the epic's user-visible ACs against a partial product; contract-first/interface units satisfy no observable AC at all, so row 16's remedy ('add rationale') asks for exactly the plan narrative that §7.4 strips.
findings.scenario: Epic E-1 (T2): U1 = migration + generated client (contract-first), U2 = API, U3 = UI. ACCEPTANCE.md: 'A1 WHEN a customer enters SAVE10 at checkout THE SYSTEM SHALL reduce the total by 10%'. S7 on U1: cold lens infers 'adds a nullable discount_pct column and regenerates the client; purpose unclear' → sep-judge: MISMATCH; customer lens: A1 FAIL (no endpoint yet) → row 11 SENDBACK S5 with 'the judge's script is the repro' — the executor cannot make a migration pass a checkout test. If the FAIL is suppressed, row 16 DEFER-GATE → executor adds `// part of the cart-discount feature (A1)` → narrative scan flags 'cart-discount' → neutralized → second MISMATCH → H3 'design problem'. Every multi-unit epic's first unit escalates to the human.
findings.fix: Pack carries `ACCEPTANCE.slice.md` = only ACs with `ac_to_units[A] == {u}` (fully satisfiable by this unit); ACs spanning several units are verified ONCE per wave by a customer lens on the integrated sandbox (base = wave base, head = integration tip after landing), and decide.sh applies rows 11–13 only to ACs in the unit's slice. M = `n/a` when the slice is empty (contract-first/interface units) and the judge instead checks `inferred_intent` against `interface.json.purpose`; rows 11–13,16 require M/Bc ≠ n/a. Row 16: MISMATCH alone is a `concern` on the merge card (T0/T1: logged to lessons; T2+: HOLD-free card line), never a second DEFER and never H3. Define the allowed rationale: product-level WHAT/WHY in a docstring is legitimate, references to cards/rounds/rulings are narrative.

findings.section: §3 S0 (ACCEPTANCE.md frozen); §9 rules ('rulings pasted into every later stage'); §7.5 ('may not: rulings'); §6 row 1
findings.claim: Rulings/H0 answers change what 'done' means, ACCEPTANCE.md is frozen, and rulings are (correctly) excluded from the blind pack — so the customer lens verifies stale acceptance text; the executor, told the ruling, changes nothing, and the 'artifact hash unchanged after a send-back' rule escalates a correct unit to H3.
findings.scenario: ACCEPTANCE.md: 'A1 … SHALL reduce the total by 10%'. H0 question 'before or after tax?' answered 'after tax' → rulings.md `R14 [E-1/U2] Q: … → A: after tax (maksat, 2026-09-26)`. Executor implements after-tax; S6 passes (has rulings). Customer lens computes 10% of the pre-tax subtotal, sees a different total → A1 FAIL with a script → row 11 SENDBACK S5. Executor reads R14, finds the code correct, commits nothing → `diff_sha256 === st.lastHash` → row 1 ESCALATE, unit parked, human wakes up for a non-defect. Pasting rulings.md into the pack instead would leak `E-1/U2`, the author's name and the fact that a question was raised.
findings.fix: Code regenerates `ACCEPTANCE.effective.md` at S0 exit and after every ruling/answer that names an AC id: the AC line with the accepted default/answer folded in as a WHAT statement ('… SHALL reduce the after-tax total by 10%'), no ruling ids, authors, dates, unit ids; MANIFEST.json tracks its inputs (ACCEPTANCE.md, answers.md, rulings.md) so a new ruling invalidates downstream S7 results for units whose slice changed. The pack ships only the effective file (verb deny-list + narrative grep applied to it). Rulings stay out of the pack.

findings.section: §7.2 step 2 strip list; §7.2 step 5 tree_hash; §6 row 13; §15 'first env failure auto-declares run:null'
findings.claim: The strip list deletes paths a legitimate change may touch (`docs/decisions`, `CHANGELOG*`, `.env*` incl. `.env.example`, `AGENTS.md`, `.github/*`), so the blind lenses judge a diff that is not the diff being merged, and stripping `.env*` makes most web apps unbootable in the sandbox, turning 'UNVERIFIABLE' into an S0 send-back for a correct change.
findings.scenario: (a) Row 16 DEFER-GATE: executor adds `docs/decisions/0007-discount-after-tax.md` as rationale; sandbox.sh strips `docs/decisions` → the second cold lens sees the same diff → MISMATCH again → H3. (b) Unit adds `DISCOUNT_ENGINE_URL` to `.env.example` and reads it at boot; sandbox has no `.env*`; `commands.run` fails → customer lens: every AC UNVERIFIABLE → row 13 SENDBACK S0 'acceptance not observable' → triage re-asks the human about ACs that were fine. Meanwhile decision.json's `diff_sha256` covers files the lenses never saw, so the merge card's 'Blind: SAFE' is about a different artifact.
findings.fix: Strip ONLY agent/funnel configuration: `.separator .claude CLAUDE*.md AGENTS.md .cursor .github/copilot* .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE*`; treat secrets by redaction (next finding), not deletion. Hard rule in sandbox.sh: `stripped ∩ files_touched(base..head) = ∅`, else the sandbox is INVALID (harness incident, row 5) — never a verdict on a partial diff; manifest records `stripped[]` and `diff_sha256_sandbox`, and decide.sh requires it to equal `sha256(git diff base..HEAD)` minus the stripped set. sandbox.sh materializes `.env` from `.env.example`/`policy.sandbox_env` with placeholder values before launch. `per_acceptance[].result = UNVERIFIABLE` carries `reason ∈ {env, unobservable, timeout}`; only `unobservable` routes to S0; `env` → rebuild once with commands.setup output attached, then `run:null` for that zone (as §15 already promises) and Bc = skipped.

findings.section: §7.2 step 6 ('cold lens → nothing') vs §7.5 ('may see build/test/run commands') vs §3 S7 ('judges must EXECUTE; empty evidence = weight 0'); §12.1 disallowedTools WebFetch/WebSearch
findings.claim: The cold lens is required to execute but is given no commands, a `git archive` tree with no installed dependencies, and (by policy) no network; so it either produces empty evidence twice (INVALID → H3 on every unit) or the Bash guard lets `npm install`/`pip install` through, which opens a full network channel (`gh issue view`, `curl` to the tracker holding the original request) that no regex guard closes.
findings.scenario: pnpm monorepo, zone `billing`. Sandbox contains package.json but no node_modules. Cold lens tries `pnpm test` → 'command not found: vitest'; tries `pnpm install` → registry blocked (or, if allowed, 90 s per lens per unit per round, and the same allow lets `curl https://api.github.com/repos/org/app/issues?labels=discount` return the ticket that is the raw request). Blocked case: evidence[] empty → check-evidence exit 2 'execute before voting' → still nothing runnable → INVALID → H3 harness incident for a perfectly good change; with two lenses × 8 T1 units this is 16 human-facing incidents per epic.
findings.fix: commands.json (build, test, run, setup — no zone names, no funnel-only `mutate`/`fast`) goes to BOTH lenses. sandbox.sh runs `commands.setup` itself before launch, seeding dependency dirs from the executor's worktree (`node_modules`, `.venv`, `vendor`, `target`, gitignored so never in the archive) by copy/hardlink, and records `setup_exit` in the manifest. The blind run then gets network OFF: Claude Code sandbox via `--settings '{"sandbox":{"enabled":true,"failIfUnavailable":false,"autoAllowBashIfSandboxed":true,"network":{"strictAllowlist":true,"allowedDomains":[]},"filesystem":{"denyRead":["<project>","~/"],"allowRead":["<sandbox>"]}}}'` when bwrap exists, else `env -i` with `HTTP_PROXY=HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 NO_PROXY=` plus a guard on `curl|wget|gh |git (fetch|clone|pull)|pip|npm|pnpm|yarn|cargo|go (get|mod)`; manifest.confinement ∈ {os, hook}. Define evidence for non-runnable products: any commands.json command with exit code (build/typecheck/lint) counts; `E = empty` is a harness INVALID only when commands.json is non-empty; observation-only units get Bk from static evidence with weight noted on the card.

findings.section: §7.2 step 4 redact.sh; §5.2 ratchet flake check; §6 rows 10–11
findings.claim: redact.sh rewrites emails/tokens inside the diff, including test fixtures, so the sandbox runs a different program than the branch; failures that exist only in the sandbox become send-backs whose repro cannot be reproduced on the branch, and the spec has no path for a repro that passes on the branch.
findings.scenario: Unit adds `fixtures/users.json` with `alice@example.com` and `test/notify.test.ts` asserting that address is emailed. redact.sh replaces the email with `<redacted-email>` in fixtures but the assertion string (a different pattern) stays → test fails only in the sandbox → customer lens A2 FAIL with the test command → row 11 SENDBACK S5. ratchet.sh runs the repro on the branch: it passes → 'fails 2× on the branch' not met → no regress test, but `sendbacks.execute` was incremented and the executor receives a defect card it cannot reproduce → commits nothing → hash unchanged → row 1 ESCALATE.
findings.fix: Redact only what the gate's secret scan classifies as a real secret (high-entropy tokens, private keys, cloud key patterns) — those should already be blocked at the gate, so the sandbox rarely needs redaction; allow-list `example.com/.test/.invalid/localhost`, RFC 2606/5737 values, and never touch files under zone `test_globs` or fixture dirs. Record every redaction in `manifest.redactions[] {file, line, kind}`. decide.sh: any blind finding whose repro output or file:line intersects `manifest.redactions` → `harness` outcome (re-run that lens on an unredacted copy, no counter charged), never a send-back. Add to selftest.sh: a fixture with a test asserting an email must PASS inside a freshly built sandbox.

findings.section: §7.4 canary and provenance; §12.4 selftest; §14 glossary ('absence … proves blindness'); §3 S2 skip rule
findings.claim: Leak detection only catches a reviewer that QUOTES the canary or reads via a tool whose argument the hook logs; Bash reads that dodge the regex are invisible, and on the T0/T1-skip lanes (~80% of units) no planner runs so no canary is planted at all — the leak-check reports 'clean' for the units it never guarded.
findings.scenario: T1 unit with 2 files and 1 zone: S2 skipped, card synthesized by code, canary never embedded. Headless cold lens (Bash unconfined, mechanics §9.5) runs `find / -name 'card.md' -newer package.json 2>/dev/null | head -1 | xargs cat` — no `..`, no `/home`, no `.separator` literal in the command → guard passes; card.md content enters the context. knowledge_statement paraphrases the goal without quoting anything; reads.log lists only the find command; `forbidden_reads[]` empty, `canary_hit=false` → verdict counted, sandbox 'audited'. The same holds with a canary present, since paraphrase ≠ quote.
findings.fix: (1) Canary is planted by `sep new-epic` (code) into every card, dag.json and the epic's request wrapper, on every lane; (2) physical read audit independent of the tool layer: during a blind run, `inotifywait -m -r -e open,access <project>/.separator/epics/<epic> <project>/.git` (fallback: snapshot `stat -c %X` atimes of those trees before/after when the FS keeps atime) writes any access to `leak-check.forbidden_reads[]`; (3) when bwrap is available, the OS sandbox `filesystem.denyRead` on the project dir and `~/` makes the audit a hard guarantee and `manifest.confinement=os`; (4) reword the glossary: the canary is a tripwire, physical confinement + read audit is the proof; (5) selftest.sh includes a Bash-based exfiltration probe (`find`/`xargs cat` of a planted file outside the sandbox) and asserts `forbidden_reads` is non-empty or the command was denied.

findings.section: §4 blind review record schema (`findings[…as above…]` incl. `origin`); §7.2 step 3 git init; §7.3 guard-blind denial text; §12.2 blindPrompt(u,l); nested-process environment
findings.claim: Several small channels tell the blind lens about the pipeline, the author or the unit: the shared findings schema asks the blind lens for `origin ∈ {code, contract, decomposition, request}` (announces contracts/decomposition and primes plan-thinking); the sandbox's two commits carry the human's global git identity; hook denial messages echo real paths; `blindPrompt(u, l)` receives the whole unit object (title, zone, writes); and the nested `claude -p` inherits the parent environment, which here contains `CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL=<the user's email>`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` (from which the parent transcript path under `~/.claude/projects/` is derivable) and would contain any `SEP_*` variables the driver exports.
findings.scenario: Cold lens runs `env | sort` as its first orientation command (common); sees the user's email and session id, then `git log --format='%an %ae'` in the sandbox shows the same person as committer → 'author identity' §7.5 forbids is known. A guard denial reads 'denied: /home/user/---/.separator/epics/E-1/blind/U2/pack is outside the sandbox' → unit id and funnel confirmed. The schema forces a `decomposition` tag choice, so the lens writes 'this seems to be one unit of a decomposed plan' in knowledge_statement — harmless for the canary, but the verdict is no longer context-free.
findings.fix: Blind schema has no `origin` (sep-router assigns it) and no `sig` computed from unit data; `git -c user.name=sep -c user.email=sep@sandbox commit` with `GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=@0`; guard messages are constant strings ('outside sandbox'); `blindPrompt` takes only `{sandbox_path, lens, prompt_sha}` and the prompt file is fixed per lens and hashed into the manifest; blind.sh launches with `env -i PATH=$PATH HOME=<sandbox>/.home TMPDIR=<sandbox>/.tmp <auth vars only> claude -p …` and selftest asserts `env` inside a blind run contains no `CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` or `SEP_*`.

findings.section: §7.2 Sandbox construction, §7.3 Launch (deny network), §7.6 customer lens, §6 row 13, §15 'first env failure auto-declares run: null once'
findings.claim: The blind sandbox is a bare `git archive` tree with no dependency provisioning and no network, so on every package-managed repo (composer/npm/pip/gradle/pods) the customer lens cannot build or run anything, and the spec's own escape hatch then disables the customer lens permanently.
findings.scenario: 10-year PHP monolith, `vendor/` gitignored, zone commands `{setup:'composer install', test:'vendor/bin/phpunit', run:'php -S localhost:8080 -t public'}`. Unit U1 passes the mechanical gate in its worktree. `sandbox.sh` extracts base+head trees (no vendor/, no .env), `guard-blind.sh` denies network. `sep-outsider-customer` runs `vendor/bin/phpunit` -> 'No such file'; `php -S` -> autoload fatal. Every AC -> UNVERIFIABLE with non-empty evidence -> row 13 SENDBACK S0 ('acceptance not observable'), `sendbacks.intake` cap 1 -> H3 on the second unit. Alternatively §15 fires: the first env failure auto-declares `run: null`, so the customer lens is skipped for every later unit in that zone and the 'second separator' collapses to the cold diff reader on essentially every real repository (same for `npm ci`, `pip install`, `pod install`, `./gradlew`, and iOS/Android device builds).
findings.fix: Add a provisioning step to `sandbox.sh` (runs WITH network, before the lens starts, outside the lens's tool set): if `commands.setup` exists run it inside the sandbox; otherwise/additionally hard-link or copy `policy.dep_dirs` (node_modules, vendor, .venv, target, Pods, .gradle, DerivedData) from the gate worktree when the lockfile blob at `head_sha` equals the worktree's; record `provisioned[]` + lockfile hashes in `manifest.json` and exclude those dirs from `leak-scan` forbidden reads and from the cold-lens diff. For builds that exceed `policy.max_gate_seconds` or need credentials (Xcode signing), let `gate.sh` produce the built artifact from `head_sha` and place it in `pack/` with its hash listed in the manifest. An environment failure inside a lens is an INVALID/harness result (row 5), never an auto-declaration of `run: null`; `run: null` may only be set by a human at Hz.

findings.section: §3 S4 outputs (`units/<u>/tests/acc_<u>.*`), §3 S5 hooks (frozen `tests/acc_*`), §4 layout (`.separator/epics/` gitignored), §12.4 guard-scope.sh
findings.claim: Acceptance/regress test placement and the frozen-test check assume a `tests/` directory with file-level globs, which Go (colocated `_test.go`), Rust (inline `#[cfg(test)]`), PHPUnit (class/file suffix rules), Swift/Android (test targets/source sets) and notebooks do not follow; and §4 puts the tests under gitignored `.separator/epics/`, where neither the unit branch, the sandbox nor CI can see them.
findings.scenario: Go service, zone `internal/cart`, `test_globs: ['**/*_test.go']`. The prober writes `.separator/epics/E1/units/U1/tests/acc_U1.go` as §4 says: `go test` never compiles it (wrong package dir, gitignored, absent from `git archive` so the blind lens 'runs contract checks' against nothing). If instead it is placed correctly at `internal/cart/acc_u1_test.go`, `guard-scope.sh` freezes it only if the glob matches, and every other `_test.go` the executor legitimately adds is denied by `test_globs` unless the card pre-declares `test_writes`. Rust: `tests/regress_<sig>` cannot freeze the `mod tests` block inside `src/cart.rs`, which is in `writes[]`, so the executor can weaken or delete inline tests and 'frozen-test diff empty' is vacuously true. PHPUnit: `acc_U1.php` is ignored by the suite unless named `*Test.php` with a matching class; `phpunit` exits 1 for 'no tests executed', which `red-proof.sh` accepts as 'fails on base'.
findings.fix: Add `zones[].test_layout: {dir_template, file_template, run_template}` (Go: `{pkg_dir}`, `acc_{unit}_test.go`, `go test {pkg} -run Acc{Unit}`; PHP: `tests/Separator`, `Acc{Unit}Test.php`, `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter Acc{Unit}Test`; Rust: `tests`, `acc_{unit}.rs`, `cargo test --test acc_{unit}`; Python: `tests`, `test_acc_{unit}.py`, `pytest {file}`). Acceptance and regress tests are committed ON the unit branch at that path and listed in `contract.json.frozen_files[]` with blob SHAs; the frozen check is `git diff base..HEAD -- <frozen_files>` empty plus blob-SHA equality. Rule for inline-test languages: acceptance/regress tests must live in separate files; any change to an inline test block inside a write-set file is emitted as a `test-delta` item that S6 must explicitly clear. `red-proof.sh` must also assert that the test was actually executed (runner reports >=1 test), not merely a non-zero exit.

findings.section: §2.1 modifiers (LOC > 400), §3 S2 exit gate (est_files ≤ 8, ≤12 units), §3 S5 gate (canned mutants on changed lines), §7.6 cold lens (diff only), §7.2 redact.sh
findings.claim: Class, unit-size caps, mutant probes and the cold lens are all computed on raw diff lines, so generated/serialized files (lockfiles, notebooks, snapshots, generated clients, minified assets) and atomic mechanical changes (codemods, formatter runs) either inflate every task to T2/T3 or make decomposition impossible.
findings.scenario: pnpm monorepo, request 'bump axios for the CVE': `package.json` x3 + `pnpm-lock.yaml` (+2,800/-2,700). Actual-diff class: LOC>400 -> +1, lockfile is a serialized/contract-shaped resource -> T2: 2 spikes, contract-checker, H1, 2 inspectors, 3 lenses, H2 (about 11 calls + 2 human touches) for a version bump; the cold lens reads a 5k-line lockfile diff -> ILLEGIBLE -> row 16 'add rationale', second time -> H3.
