Data-science repo: re-executing a notebook changes thousands of JSON output lines (every edit is T2), canned 'flip comparison' mutants are applied to JSON, and `redact.sh` (tokens/emails) lets dataframe outputs with customer rows into the blind sandbox. Codemod: 'rename UserId -> AccountId across 40 packages' is one atomic `jscodeshift` run touching 120 files; `est_files ≤ 8` can never hold, the planner is re-invoked once, fails again -> H3 for every mechanical refactor.
findings.fix: Add `zones[].generated_globs[]` and optional `normalize_cmd` (e.g. `nbstripout`, `jq -S`): excluded from LOC/file counts, from mutant probes and from the cold-lens diff (rendered as one summary line + hash). Add unit `kind: 'regen'` with `regen_cmd`: the gate re-runs `regen_cmd` from base (+ the unit's hand-edited files) and asserts `git diff --stat` is empty, i.e. the diff is reproducible; regen units are exempt from `est_files`/`est_lines`/12-unit caps and keep the path floor (T1 unless a `risk_paths` hit), and reviewers are shown the command plus the hand-edited files only. Notebooks: `redact.sh` strips cell outputs unless the zone sets `outputs_are_artifacts: true`.

findings.section: §3 S1 (`commands.test`), §3 S5 mechanical gate, §8.8 suite latency, §6 row 22, §9 H4 promotion, §12.4 CI job
findings.claim: Every check is a local shell command; there is no check kind for verification that only exists in CI (services, secrets, 40-minute matrices) and no path for a protected `main`/`integration` that requires PRs and non-bot approvals, so such repos degrade to observation-only HOLDs and a human merge card per unit.
findings.scenario: Django app; tests need Postgres, Redis and secrets present only in GitHub Actions (40-min run); `main` is protected (PR + required checks + 1 human review). Locally `commands.test` = null -> S1b prober tries to write characterization tests, cannot connect to a DB, degrades to `observation`, class +1 -> every unit, including a T0 typo, is row 22 HOLD -> merge card -> human touch (the 'on the loop for 80%' promise is gone). `auto-merge to integration` assumes a pushable unprotected branch; 'integration -> main promoted by the human' cannot be a `git push` at all. §13 L0 even says bot approvals do not count, but nothing tells `sep-promote` to open a PR.
findings.fix: Add check kind `ci`: `{kind:'ci', workflow, ref_template}` -> `gate.sh` pushes the unit branch (guard-bash allows pushing `sep/*` branches only), triggers/polls the check-run via `gh`, records run URL + conclusion in `gate.json`; it counts as `check` (exit-code gate), not `observation`. Latency policy: `ci` checks run once per wave on the integrated tip (units gate on `fast` + local checks) with a `policy.ci_wait_max_min` budget. `sep-promote` opens a PR `integration -> main` whose body is the merge-card stack, with `separator-gate` as a required check; document that `integration` must be a pushable unprotected branch (or `integration/<user>` when the org protects all long-lived branches).

findings.section: §4 (`epics/` and `locks.json` gitignored), §8.4–8.5 (integration branch, locks), §9 H2 (alternate owner approves), §12.6, §13 L2
findings.claim: The ledger, locks, merge cards and `MERGE_APPROVED` live in gitignored directories and `integration` is a local branch, so with more than one human (or Claude Code + Cursor on the same repo) approvals, locks and integration cannot be shared and the two `integration` branches race to `main`.
findings.scenario: Three developers. A (Claude Code) runs epic E1; B is the `alternate_owner` for `billing` and is asked to approve H2: the merge card and the `MERGE_APPROVED` path exist only under A's gitignored `.separator/epics/E1/`. C (Cursor, L2 `sep.sh`) starts E2 on the same zone; `locks.json` is local to A, so no lock is seen and both write `src/billing/**`. Each funnel auto-merges T1 units to its own local `integration`; at H4 two divergent `integration` branches are pushed to `main`, the second promotion is a conflicting merge outside any counted round, and every `decision.json` hash references branches nobody else has fetched.
findings.fix: Define `policy.mode: 'solo' | 'shared'`. In shared mode: `integration` is a remote branch, landings use `git push --force-with-lease` with a bounded `integration_push_retries` counter (≤3 -> H3); the ledger subset needed by other people (`state.json`, `decision.json`, `merge-cards/`, `MERGE_APPROVED`, `CONTRACTS_APPROVED`, `locks.json`) is stored on an orphan `sep/ledger` branch (or mirrored into the unit PR body/labels), read fresh at S3/S8; approval = a commit on `sep/ledger` by a login listed in `zones.json` owners, or a GitHub review by such a human; `.gitignore` keeps only `sandbox/`, `pack/`, worktrees and `selftest.json`; §8.10 'one driver per repo per epic' becomes enforceable via the shared locks.

findings.section: §3 S4 exit gate (red-proof.sh), §3 S5 gate ('Skip: never for code changes', mutants), §6 row 22, §7.6 customer lens ('runs the product'), §13
findings.claim: Docs-only, design-only and pure-research tasks have no defined path: the prober's Stop hook demands a failing test, the gate demands mutants and commands, row 22 HOLDs every observation-only unit, and the customer lens is told to run a product that does not exist.
findings.scenario: Request A: 'rewrite the onboarding docs' (600 lines under `docs/`). Actual diff LOC>400 -> T2 modifiers -> premortem, 2 spikes, contract-checker, H1, H2 for prose. Request B: 'research Kafka vs NATS for our event bus and recommend one' (no code output). S4: `sep-prober` must produce a FAILING acceptance test and `red-proof.sh` refuses its stop until one exists -> loops, then `status: fail`. If the planner declares all checks `observation`, S5's `require-evidence.sh` and `gate.sh` have no defined behaviour for null commands, 'each mutant must make a test fail' is evaluated on a `.md`, and row 22 HOLDs the unit -> human merge card for every paragraph. The customer lens prompt ('run it, test each criterion') has nothing to run.
findings.fix: Add `deliverable: 'code' | 'content' | 'research'` at unit level (zone default). content: checks are `lint|links|render|spell` commands (kind `check`); mutants, frozen-tests and `red-proof` are skipped by kind; size modifiers use file counts; T0/T1 may auto-merge when checks are green and the cold lens is SAFE; the customer lens reads the rendered artefact and scores each AC. research: the contract is the question list derived from ACCEPTANCE; the executor emits `findings.md` with `[claim] <- source#anchor` lines; gate = `cite-check.sh` (every claim resolves to a source excerpt; `sep-verifier` re-fetches/greps a sample); red-proof becomes 'questions unanswered on base'; the cold lens back-translates 'what question does this answer' for the intent MATCH; row 22 does not apply because citation check is a `check`.

findings.section: §3 S3/S5 (worktree per unit, WIP ≤5), §8.2–8.4, §12.4 hooks (no WorktreeCreate), zones.json `commands.setup`
findings.claim: Parallel worktrees share one dev database, one port range, one simulator and one docker daemon, and nothing in the spec runs `commands.setup` per worktree or accounts for its cost, so parallel units corrupt each other's test runs and the first `fast` gate fails in every fresh worktree.
findings.scenario: Rails/Django repo with `DATABASE_URL=postgres://localhost/app_dev`; wave of 4 units in 4 worktrees, U2 is a migration unit (serialized resource `migrations` covers the files only). All four executors run `commands.test` concurrently against the same `app_dev`; U2's migration lands mid-suite for U1/U3 -> their tests fail, flake control re-runs them 2x in isolation -> they pass -> 'quarantined as flaky' and the ledger is poisoned; `commands.run` on :3000 from 4 worktrees -> three EADDRINUSE. Separately: each worktree starts without `node_modules`/`.venv`/`target`/`Pods`; the executor's first `fast` command fails inside the Stop hook 3x -> `status: fail` -> a burned retry; if the agent runs setup itself, 5 concurrent `cargo build`/`pod install`/`npm ci` on a laptop take 10-20 min each and exhaust `maxTurns`, so the parallelism that justifies the funnel's speed claim makes it slower.
findings.fix: Add `zones[].exclusive_resources[]` (e.g. `db:app_dev`, `port:3000`, `ios-simulator`) distinct from write-set `serialized_resources`: `gate.sh`, `require-evidence.sh` and the customer lens wrap `test|run|smoke` in a portable `mkdir`-based lock per resource; zones that can isolate declare `isolation: per_unit` and `commands.setup/test/run` receive `SEP_UNIT`, `SEP_PORT`, `SEP_DB_SUFFIX` templates. Add a `WorktreeCreate` hook (documented event) that runs `commands.setup` once per worktree, reusing `policy.dep_dirs` via hard-links when the lockfile blob is unchanged; record `setup_seconds` and set WIP = min(5, harness cap, floor(policy.max_parallel_setup_seconds / setup_seconds)).

findings.section: §2.1 (T3 on 'new zone'), §3 S1 (exit gate `confidence != unmapped`, Hz batched into H4), §3 S1 cartography seeded from `git log`, §8.2 worktree from `base_sha`, §12.3 `/sep init`
findings.claim: A fresh or greenfield repository either crashes (unborn HEAD) or runs every task at T3 with a design panel, because 'new zone' is a T3 signal and zone declarations wait for the daily digest.
findings.scenario: `git init` yesterday, `pyproject.toml`, 3 commits, no CI. First epic: 'build the CLI skeleton, config loader and tests'. `sep zones init` produces one inferred zone; the planner introduces `src/cli/` and `src/config/` -> 'new zone' -> T3: three `sep-designer`s + two judges + H1 + H2 + rollback plan for a hello-world CLI, and the S1 exit gate ('every path maps to a zone with confidence != unmapped') cannot pass until the Hz declaration, which is 'batched into the H4 digest' (daily). With a repo that has zero commits (`git init` only), `git worktree add` and `git archive <base_sha>` fail on the unborn HEAD and the workflow throws at S3.
findings.fix: `/sep init` creates an initial commit when HEAD is unborn and writes a catch-all zone `{paths:['**'], confidence:'inferred', risk_floor:'T1', commands from detected build files or null}`. The 'new zone' T3 modifier applies only when the map already has ≥1 `declared` zone and the unit ADDS a zone; in greenfield the planner proposes zones in `zones.patch.json` at floor T1. An unmapped path that blocks the current epic is asked in the H0 packet immediately, with the inferred zone as the default so T0/T1 proceed under `assumptions[]`; only steady-state declarations go to the digest. Cartographer churn seeding is optional: empty `git log` -> build-file inference only.

findings.section: §3 S8 verdict record (`diff_sha256 = sha256(git diff base..HEAD)`), §12.4 guard-bash / `.githooks/pre-push` / CI `separator-gate`, §13 enforcement floor
findings.claim: `git diff` output depends on per-machine git configuration and object-database size, so the verdict hash recomputed by pre-push or CI differs from the one recorded, and the enforcement floor that non-Claude tools rely on rejects unchanged code.
findings.scenario: Verified locally (git 2.43): on identical commits, `sha256(git diff A B)` differs between `core.abbrev=7` and `core.abbrev=12` and between `diff.renames=true/false` (the `index abc1234..def5678` lines and rename detection are part of the bytes). `core.abbrev` defaults to 'auto', which scales with the number of objects, so a shallow CI clone on Ubuntu and the developer's full clone on macOS produce different diffs for the same `base..HEAD`; a Windows teammate with `diff.algorithm=histogram` in the global config differs again. Result: `separator-gate` and the pre-push hook report 'code changed after the verdict' on every PR, blocking all pushes; the CI job that is supposed to work 'with zero AI tooling' is red by construction.
findings.fix: Define the verdict hash on git's own content identifiers: `base_tree = git rev-parse <base_sha>^{tree}`, `head_tree = git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`, `diff_sha256 = sha256(base_tree + '\n' + head_tree)` (config- and OS-independent; any content change changes the tree id). If a textual diff is wanted for humans, produce it with a pinned canonical command (`git -c diff.renames=false -c diff.algorithm=myers -c core.abbrev=40 diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --full-index --no-textconv <base> <head>`) but never hash it. `selftest.sh` asserts the hash matches between the working checkout and a fresh `git clone --depth 1`.

findings.section: §1 principle 13, §3 S0 exit gate (verb deny-list), §3 S5 gate (skip markers, canned mutations), §2.1 size thresholds, §12.4/§13 (`bin/sep` bash+jq), §3 S1 commands
findings.claim: Several language-, locale- and platform-specific constants are hard-coded outside `zones.json`/`policy.json`, contradicting the 'universality lives in one file' principle and silently disabling guards for non-English requests, other languages and Windows.
findings.scenario: The user writes requests in Russian; triage writes `ACCEPTANCE.md` in Russian ('СИСТЕМА ДОЛЖНА переименовать таблицу и закэшировать …'); the English deny-list `refactor|extract|use a|add table|migrate|rename|cache` never matches, so the implementation-verb guard is off without anyone noticing. The skip-marker scan (`skip/only/todo`) misses `markTestSkipped`, `t.Skip(`, `#[ignore]`, `@Disabled`, `xit(`; canned mutations have no per-language syntax and a mutant that fails to compile counts as 'killed'; T0's '≤80 lines' means very different work in Java vs Python. A Windows developer in Git Bash without `jq` or `flock` gets `gate.sh: jq: command not found`, which `selftest.sh` does not check, so the gate refuses to run and the funnel never starts. A 40-package monorepo zone cannot express `cwd` or affected-only selection (`turbo run test --filter=...[${BASE_SHA}]`) because commands are fixed strings.
findings.fix: Move the constants: `policy.ac_verb_denylist` keyed by language (EN + RU defaults, auto-selected from the request's script); `zones[].lang` selects `bin/lang.d/<lang>.json` holding `skip_markers[]`, `mutations[]` (each verified with `commands.build`; non-compiling mutants count as `not_applied`), `test_layout`, and `size_thresholds`; zone commands gain `cwd` and `${SEP_BASE_SHA}`, `${SEP_CHANGED_FILES}`, `${SEP_UNIT}` templates. `selftest.sh` asserts prerequisites (git ≥ 2.38 for `merge-tree --write-tree`, `jq` or a python3/node fallback, a sha256 tool, tar), hooks invoke scripts as `bash "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/..."` so the executable bit is irrelevant on Windows checkouts, and locks use `mkdir` instead of `flock`.

findings.section: §12.3 skills (`sep` has disable-model-invocation), §12.5 CLAUDE.md, §12.4 guard-scope deny list, §3 S0 'Who', §12.2 sep-intake.js args
findings.claim: A plain typed request has no defined, hook-legal path into the funnel: the model may not invoke `/sep`, CLAUDE.md invites the main session to straight-line small edits, and the only writers of `request.md` are all denied.
findings.scenario: Day 2, user types 'fix the 500 on empty cart at checkout'. Main session reads CLAUDE.md: 'work directly for single-file edits; run /sep' — `sep` is `disable-model-invocation`, so the model cannot run it and edits cart.ts directly: the exact task→error→fix line the user wanted to escape, with no gate and no lens. If the user does type `/sep fix the 500...`, the driver must create `.separator/epics/<e>/request.md`, but guard-scope (global PreToolUse Edit|Write) denies `request.md`/`ACCEPTANCE.md` as gate files, guard-bash denies redirects into protected paths, `sep-triage` has no write tools, and scripts 'have no filesystem access'; `sep-intake.js` takes `{epic, ts, answers_sha}` and no request text. The user's first experience is a hook denial or a silent bypass of the funnel.
findings.fix: (1) One entry point: `/sep <text>` (or `sep-batch` for many) is THE way work enters; add a `UserPromptSubmit` hook that, when `.separator/` exists and the prompt is not a slash command or `!`-prefixed, injects 'route this through the sep-intake skill; the main session never edits source files'. Remove `disable-model-invocation` from the intake entry (keep it on promote/revert/rule). (2) Add `bin/sep new-epic "<text>"` that mints the epic id, writes `request.md` verbatim, `chmod a-w`, and returns the path; the driver calls only this. (3) guard-scope/guard-bash apply only when stdin `agent_type` starts with `sep-` or `cwd` is under `.claude/worktrees/`; the driver (agent_type absent) may write `.separator/epics/**` except unit outputs. (4) CLAUDE.md line becomes 'single-file edits go through the T0 lane (one executor + one cold lens, ~3 calls); the main session never edits source; to bypass, prefix `!`.'

findings.section: §12.2 driver ('writes returned JSON to the run dir'; 'scripts hold counters'), §8.5, §5.5 'nothing green is re-run on resume', §3 S3 contract staleness
findings.claim: State is persisted only when a workflow script returns, so closing the laptop mid-`sep-build.js` leaves `state.json` stale; `/sep` then relaunches the wave from scratch and re-implements units already merged to integration.
findings.scenario: T1 epic, 6 units in 2 waves. 25 min into `sep-build.js`, U1 and U2 have been merged to `integration` by the integrator agent (real git state), U3's executor is mid-edit; the laptop closes. `state.json` still says all units 'not started' (counters lived in script memory). Next morning the user types `/sep`: the driver reads stale state and launches a NEW run (the spec never tells the user to resume a runId via `/workflows`). U1/U2 get fresh executors on a base that already contains their code → the RED-on-base recheck now passes on base → 'contract no longer fails → S4 revise' → prober rewrites tests → integrator merges a second implementation onto integration that already has the first → conflict → `integration_rounds` → H3. A morning burned with no defect anywhere.
findings.fix: (1) Every `bin/` script an agent runs (gate.sh, sandbox.sh, ratchet.sh, `bin/sep merge`) appends `{unit, stage, round, head_sha, runId}` to `epics/<e>/events.jsonl`; the driver records the workflow runId in `state.json` at launch. (2) `/sep` always runs `bin/sep reconcile <epic>` first: derives per-unit state from git (existing `sep/<e>/<u>` branches + `Separator-Unit:` trailers on integration = merged) plus events.jsonl, rewrites state.json, and prints a 5-line resume summary ('U1,U2 merged · U3 half-built (3 commits) · U4–U6 not started — resume run <id>? [y]'); it never dispatches a unit whose trailer is on integration. (3) Executor prompt: 'if branch sep/<e>/<u> exists, check it out in your worktree and continue from notes.md; never recreate it.'

findings.section: §12.4 SessionStart status.sh, §12.2 'scripts hold counters', §9 notifications via `Notification` hook
findings.claim: During the longest script the user cannot learn what is happening: the status board renders only at SessionStart from a stale state.json, the workflow occupies the session in the foreground, and packet-ready notifications are hung on a hook event that fires on permission/idle, not on files.
findings.scenario: User launches a T2 epic; `sep-build.js` runs ~45 min. The workflow UI shows phase 'Execute' and labels like 'U3 r1'. The user asks (as in this very session) 'дай статус что происходит' — the session is busy, so the answer comes only after the run; pressing Esc interrupts the workflow (→ resume problem above). From a second terminal `status.sh` prints the pre-run state. When the merge card is finally written, no notification arrives because the `Notification` hook never fired.
findings.fix: (1) Scripts `log()` one fixed-format line per transition: 'U3 · execute r1 ✔ gate ✔ → inspect (2 lenses) · elapsed 12m · next human gate: merge card ≈ 20m'. (2) `bin/sep status` (shell, no LLM) reads events.jsonl + git and prints the board from any terminal; the driver tells the user up front: 'this runs unattended ~N min (from metrics); you can close the laptop, `/sep` resumes; cards land in .separator/epics/<e>/merge-cards/'. (3) Notify via the driver after each script returns and via a `SubagentStop` hook on `sep-judge`/integrator writes, calling `notify.sh` with `policy.notify`; drop the `Notification`-hook claim.

findings.section: §3 S5 'Who' (`permissionMode: acceptEdits`), §12.1 agent table, §12.4 hooks, §12.4 selftest ('bypassPermissions not set')
findings.claim: Nothing pre-approves the Bash commands the funnel's subagents run, so every test/lint/git/gate command surfaces a permission prompt to the human in the interactive session — the human is IN the loop clicking Yes for the whole run.
findings.scenario: T1 epic, 4 units on a pnpm repo. Each executor runs `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `git add`/`git commit` (×3 attempts); the verifier runs `.separator/bin/gate.sh`; `sandbox.sh`; two blind lenses run `pnpm test` and `curl`; the inspector re-runs gates. `acceptEdits` covers file edits only; the spec defines no `permissions.allow`. Result: 40–60 Bash approval prompts in one epic, each blocking the run until the user answers; the tempting escape, `bypassPermissions`, is exactly what selftest forbids.
findings.fix: `/sep init` generates `.claude/settings.json` `permissions.allow` from `zones.json` commands and the harness (`Bash(pnpm test:*)`, `Bash(pnpm lint:*)`, `Bash(git add:*)`, `Bash(git commit:*)`, `Bash(git worktree:*)`, `Bash(.separator/bin/*)`) plus `deny` for push/reset/checkout; guard-bash returns `permissionDecision: allow` for allow-listed commands and `deny` for the dangerous ones so no decision reaches the human; selftest adds 'a fixture unit completes with zero permission prompts'. Blind lenses launched headless keep `--allowedTools`.

findings.section: §3 S8 Merge, §8.5 integration order, §9 H4, §12.1 sep-integrator 'worktree of integration'
findings.claim: The spec never says which branch the human's working copy sits on; on `main` the user sees none of the auto-merged T0/T1 work until H4, and on `integration` the integrator's 'worktree of integration' cannot be created because the branch is checked out.
findings.scenario: User's checkout is `main` with `pnpm dev` running. T0 request 'rename Checkout button to Pay' → 6 min later 'merged to integration'. Browser refresh: nothing changed. The user retypes the request → a second epic (no dedupe) → duplicate unit → conflict at integration. Alternative: the user switches to `integration` to see results; now `git worktree add ... integration` fails ('already checked out'), so every merge in the epic fails and lands in `integration_rounds` → H3.
findings.fix: State the solo branch model explicitly: the human's checkout IS `integration` (dev server runs on it); `main` is the promoted line. `bin/sep merge <unit>` runs in the main checkout (`git -C $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR merge --no-ff sep/<e>/<u>`), refuses only when the dirty tree overlaps the unit's write-set (then queues and tells the user), so T0/T1 results appear in the running app within minutes; the driver prints 'landed on integration — visible now; `/sep revert U1` to undo'. H4 promotion = `git push origin integration:main` (or a PR). Offer `policy.human_branch` for users who insist on `main`, with the integrator path adjusted.

findings.section: §9 H1, §2.1 T2 row, §10 cost model (1 touch for T2)
findings.claim: For a solo user H1 is a hard serial stop in the middle of every T2 epic: plan → wait for human → build → wait for human, so wall-clock is bounded by two human return latencies and the acceleration promise fails on the 15% of tasks that matter most.
findings.scenario: 18:00, solo dev types a T2 request (touches billing). Intake 2 min, plan+spike 10 min → contracts packet at 18:12; the user has left. Epic parked until 09:00 → build 40 min → merge card 09:45 → user in a meeting → merge at 11:00. A straight-line chat would have produced code by 18:30. Batching does not help: there is one epic. `auto_approve_after_h` 'set per zone by the owner' and 'alternate owner' are team concepts with no meaning when owner = alternate = the one user.
findings.fix: For T2 (never T3, never a unit with `irreversible[] != []`), execution proceeds speculatively past H1 in worktrees — nothing reaches integration without H2 anyway. When the human returns, H1 and H2 are one packet ('contracts + result'); an H1 edit discards the affected branches (tokens are the accepted price per §10). Collapse owner/alternate to a single `policy.solo: true` default that sets this behaviour and hides the per-zone owner fields.

findings.section: §5.2 ratchet, §6 rows 10/14, §5.4 counter reset, §9 H3, §12.4 guard-scope (frozen `tests/regress_*`)
findings.claim: The human cannot dispute a reviewer finding until two full rounds have burned and the ratchet has already frozen the reviewer's repro as a permanent hook-protected test; nothing at H3 retires that test or clears its sig.
findings.scenario: Inspector files `fix` with repro 'POST /checkout code=-10 must return 400' (no AC asked for negative-code validation). Row 10: ratchet writes `tests/regress_<sig>` (frozen) BEFORE re-dispatch. Executor either implements unrequested behaviour or, per its prompt ('if a test is wrong, stop and say so'), reports blocked → round 2 → `sendbacks.execute` exhausted → H3. The human writes a ruling 'negative codes are not a requirement', but the frozen test stays in the tree (executors are hook-denied from touching it; the human is never told to delete it), the sig stays in `sigs_seen`, and the next unit in that zone inherits the wrong gate. ~20 min of tokens before the user even saw the disagreement.
findings.fix: (1) `/sep dispute <sig> "<reason>"` plus a `[drop finding]` option on stuck and merge cards: `bin/sep retire-sig` moves `tests/regress_<sig>` to `tests/retired/`, appends the ruling, removes the sig from `sigs_seen`, and adds the claim to the epic's 'do not re-litigate' list pasted to inspectors. (2) `policy.watch` (default on for solo): the driver posts a one-line notice with the repro on the FIRST send-back; a dispute within that round cancels the ratchet and re-dispatch. (3) Optionally, the ratchet keeps the test `pending` (not frozen) until a second role (executor evidence or verifier) confirms it fails on the branch.

findings.section: §3 S0 (`intent` assumptions acked at H4), §9 H4 packet, §9.1, §3 S8 `/sep revert` logs an escape
findings.claim: Intent assumptions on T1 reach the human only at the daily digest, after the code is merged and in use, with 'ack' as the only non-destructive option; the digest itself is a wall of cards the user will rubber-stamp.
findings.scenario: Tuesday 10:00: T1 unit 'apply discount code' defaulted `intent: discount applies after tax` and auto-merged; the user tested the app on integration all day. Wednesday H4: 14 merge cards (~170 lines) + 6 assumptions + 3 Hz declarations + 2 tuning proposals + 'no escapes logged: true or unlogged?'. The user disagrees with 'after tax'. Options are promote / revert / ack / apply proposal: revert logs an escape (billing floor +1 for 10 tasks) for what was a defaulted question, and no path creates the corrected unit — the user must retype a request. 'Unlogged?' asks the human something they cannot know.
findings.fix: (1) `intent`-tagged assumptions on T1 are posted as a one-line notice at merge time ('assumed: discount after tax — `/sep rule` to change'), not held for H4. (2) H4 adds `reject assumption → amendment`, which opens a compensating unit via §5.6 and logs no escape; `sep-revert --taste` reverts without an escape. (3) Digest = one line per merged unit (intent · risk · reviewers' verdicts · files), cards expandable by unit id; assumptions deduped by text; Hz as 'declare all inferred zones [y]'; replace the 'unlogged?' prompt with the auto-detector's count.

findings.section: §11 shadow mode, §13 day-one adoption, §12.3 (no `sep-init` skill), §12.4 selftest at SessionStart/ConfigChange + gate refusal, mechanics §9.1 (agents registered at session start only)
findings.claim: Day one is unspecified and hostile: `/sep init` is referenced but not defined, the mandatory restart is never mentioned, selftest fires an LLM call at session start and can lock every gate, and shadow mode makes the user do ten tasks twice with a baseline nobody measures.
findings.scenario: User runs `/sep init` on a 200k-line monorepo. Agents written to `.claude/agents` are invisible until restart (verified), so the first `/sep` throws 'agent type sep-triage not found' or silently falls back to a generic agent. The ConfigChange hook fires selftest immediately; its cold-lens fixture needs the not-yet-registered agent → `selftest.json` = failed → `gate.sh` refuses to run anywhere. Then shadow mode: 'produce merge cards without merging while the human works as before' → the user implements each of the first 10 tasks by hand AND pays for the funnel, receives no merged output, and the 'baseline' (their straight-line wall-clock and escapes) is never recorded because nothing instruments the manual chat. Abandoned on day 2.
findings.fix: (1) Define `/sep init`: writes inferred zones, policy, hooks, agents, permissions.allow, .gitignore, `core.hooksPath`; ends with 'restart Claude Code, then run /sep selftest' and an 8-line first-run guide (what to type, where results land, what a card is). (2) Selftest: the no-LLM checks (hook denial, schema rejection, counter fixture, stop-hook fixture) run in <10 s from the driver before the day's first launch, never at SessionStart; the canary cold-lens check is `sep selftest --full`, weekly; a failed selftest warns and raises every class by one instead of refusing. (3) Replace shadow mode with a training-wheels lane: the first 10 tasks run the funnel for real (the user gets working code) at ≥T1 with H2 for everything (nothing auto-merges); baseline from git history (`fix`/`revert` commits per task over the last 30 days) or explicitly 'no baseline'.

findings.section: §9.1 merge card, §5.5 stuck card, §14 glossary
findings.claim: Human packets speak the spec's internal vocabulary (T2, lenses, HOLD, sig, mutants, ⊆, skim, calls 9/24) and never say what each button will do; the glossary lives inside a 900-line document the user will not read.
findings.scenario: First merge card: 'class T2 (floor: billing) · Inspector (2 lenses) · Blind: customer PASS, cold SAFE, intent MATCH · HOLD: none · sig 4f2a · mutants 3/3 killed · writes ⊆ set ✔ · Skim → deferred.md · calls 9/24'. A stuck card says 'counter tripped: sendbacks.execute 2/2'. The user, whose mental model is task→error→fix, does not know whether 'send back' costs money, where 'approve' puts the code, or what a HOLD is, and guesses.
findings.fix: Render cards in plain words: 'Risk: high (touches billing)'; 'Reviewed by: 2 reviewers with context (pass) · 2 reviewers without context (pass) · their reading of the change matches your request'; 'Unresolved warnings: none'; '1 defect found and fixed in review (empty cart → 500; now a permanent test)'; 'Left for later: hard-coded 10% string'; footer 'approve = lands on integration (visible in your app) · send back = one more fix round with your note · kill = branch deleted, nothing merged'. Stage numbers, counters and sigs go to a `details.md`; `/sep help <word>` prints the §14 entry in RU/EN; never show S-/H-/Hz labels to the human.

findings.section: §3 S5 mechanical gate (lines 239-241: `git diff --name-only base..HEAD ⊆ writes[]`, `frozen-test diff empty`); §12.4 guard-scope
findings.claim: The authoritative scope and frozen-test checks read only the committed diff with default rename detection, so a rename out of a protected path and any uncommitted working-tree edit are invisible to the gate while still affecting the test run.
findings.scenario: Verified with git 2.43 defaults: executor runs `git mv core/auth.ts src/allowed/auth.ts` (source outside writes[]) and commits; `git diff --name-only base..HEAD` prints only `src/allowed/auth.ts` (`--name-status` shows `R100 core/auth.ts src/allowed/auth.ts`), so S=yes and `core/auth.ts` is deleted from the repo inside a unit that was never allowed to touch it. Second path: executor edits `tests/acc_u1.py` via Bash `sed -i` (guard-scope matches only Edit|Write; guard-bash is 'best effort'), does NOT commit it, commits only source; gate.sh runs the suite in the executor's dirty worktree → green; `git diff base..HEAD -- tests/` is empty → 'frozen tests untouched ✔' on the merge card. T0 has no S6; the tampering surfaces only at S8's integration gate as a 'regression', charged to integration_rounds with the wrong origin.
findings.fix: gate.sh (and the S6 re-run) must (1) execute in a fresh detached worktree at HEAD (`git worktree add --detach <tmp> <head_sha>`), or refuse to run unless `git status --porcelain --ignored=no` is empty and `git stash list` is empty in the unit worktree; (2) compute scope with `git diff --name-status --no-renames base..HEAD` (or `-M` and include BOTH sides of R/C rows) so sources of renames/copies count against writes[]; (3) record `gate.json.head_sha` and `gate.json.tree_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD^{tree})` so later stages can prove they tested the same tree. Add a selftest fixture for both attacks.

findings.section: §12.2 sketch line 705 (`agent('Run gate.sh…', {agentType:'sep-verifier', schema:GATE})`), §12.2 'Scripts have no filesystem access', §3 S5 'gate.json which agents cannot write', §12.4 guard-scope deny list (line 745)
findings.claim: Every 'code, 0 calls' gate result enters the workflow as an LLM's structured output, and decision.json is missing from the global deny list, so the merge hook trusts a file any sep-* agent with Edit can write.
findings.scenario: Zone `full` suite takes 5 minutes (policy.max_gate_seconds default 600 permits it). sep-verifier runs `gate.sh` through the Bash tool whose default timeout is 120 s → the command is killed, gate.json is never written, and the agent must still satisfy `schema:GATE`: it returns `{pass:false}` (row 2 → exec_retries → S2 for a harness reason) or, reading a partial log, `{pass:true}`. Conversely: sep-integrator has `Read, Edit, Bash(git *)`; guard-scope's gate-file deny list is `gate.json, state.json, MANIFEST.json, request.md, ACCEPTANCE.md` — `decision.json` is absent, so the integrator (or any agent) can Edit `decision.json.diff_sha256` to the current diff hash and guard-bash lets `git merge` into integration through. CI `separator-gate` only 'recomputes diff hash, validates schemas, requires decision.json', so it passes too.
findings.fix: (1) Run gate.sh from a GLOBAL SubagentStop hook branching on `agent_type == sep-executor` (hooks have their own `timeout`, are not agent-mediated, and per mechanics §9.2/§9.3 must live in settings.json, not frontmatter); the hook writes gate.json with `head_sha` and `attest = sha256(canonical_json + selftest.json.settings_hash + hook nonce file outside CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR)`. (2) guard-bash on `git merge|push` to integration/main recomputes everything itself: gate.json.pass && gate.json.head_sha == unit HEAD && decision.json.diff_sha256 == sha256(git diff base..HEAD) && attest valid; otherwise exit 2. (3) Add `decision.json, gate.json, contract.json, contract-check.json, spike.json, leak-check.json, manifest.json` and all `frozen[]` paths to the global Edit|Write|MultiEdit deny for every `sep-*` agent_type (only hooks/scripts write them). (4) The agent that 'returns gate.json' gets `tools: Read` only; its output is advisory, and the workflow re-checks it against the attested file at the next boundary via `/sep`. (5) CI `separator-gate` re-runs gate.sh, not just schema validation.

findings.section: §3 S5 mechanical gate lines 241-243 (canned mutations), §3 S4 red-proof 'fails for the right reason', §2.1 T0 lane, §9.1 'mutants 3/3 killed'
findings.claim: The three canned mutations both over-count kills (a mutant that fails to compile is 'killed' by every test) and, in under-tested code, block every T0/T1 unit forever because the executor cannot add the test that would kill the survivor; combined with a red-proof that cannot tell 'red because the symbol does not exist' from 'red because behaviour is wrong', an untested stub can reach S6 as 'mutants 3/3 killed'.
findings.scenario: (A) Rust/Go/TS zone: 'return constant' applied to `fn total(&self) -> Result<Money, Err>` yields `return 0` → build fails → suite exits nonzero → counted as killed; 'flip comparison' inside a template string/comment → same. Merge card prints 'mutants 3/3 killed' with zero real coverage. (B) Prober under maxTurns writes `from app.discount import apply` + `assert apply is not None`: red on base (ImportError) passes red-proof; executor ships `def apply(*a): return None`; in a compiled language the return-constant mutant does not compile → 'killed' → green to S6. (C) The user's legacy monolith: zone has `commands.test` non-null but the changed file has no tests; one-line T0 fix → 3 mutants survive → E6 block; card has no `test_writes`, zone `test_globs` are frozen, so the executor cannot add a killing test → exec_retries exhausted → S2 → planner re-plans the same unit → H3. Every T0 in an uncovered file jams. (D) Mutants run the full zone suite 3 more times → 4× suite_seconds, blowing `max_gate_seconds` on exactly the large repos the spec targets.
findings.fix: gate.json.mutants becomes `{applied, killed, survived, invalid}` where `invalid` = build/collection failed or test count differs from the baseline run; only `killed` counts and `invalid` is reported as 'no mutant evidence'. A survivor blocks only when the unit ran S4 and the mutated line is in a file the acceptance test imports/exercises (use `commands.coverage` when declared, else the import graph of `contract.json.frozen[]`); otherwise set `coverage_gap: true`, which forbids T0 auto-merge (routes to one S6 lens) and auto-grants the executor `test_writes: ["<zone test dir>/unit_<u>_*"]` flagged as test-delta for S6. Run mutants only against the acceptance test + tests in changed packages, never the full suite. red-proof.sh records `red_kind: compile|import|assert|other` in `contract.json.red_evidence`; a compile/import red is accepted only when the card lists the missing symbol in `new_symbols[]` AND the test file contains ≥1 assertion referencing each `checks[].expect` literal (grep), which S6 gets as a mandatory 'assertion strength' item.

findings.section: §3 S4 line 214 (`units/<u>/tests/acc_<u>.*` 'in the zone's convention'), §3 S5 line 230 (frozen = `tests/acc_*`, `tests/regress_*`, zone `test_globs`), §5.2 ratchet, §12.4 guard-scope
findings.claim: The frozen set is defined by path globs that assume a root `tests/` directory, so in languages whose tests must live next to the code the acceptance test is not frozen at all, and golden/snapshot/fixture files that tests depend on are never protected.
findings.scenario: Go repo, inferred zone with `test_globs: []`. Prober writes `internal/cart/acc_u2_test.go` (it must be in the package to run under `go test`). guard-scope's `tests/acc_*` glob does not match, `test_globs` is empty → the executor edits the assertion to its own (wrong) output → 'frozen-test diff empty' ✓, the tautological assertion kills all mutants ✓, gate green. Variant: `testdata/order.golden` is inside the unit's `writes[]` glob `internal/cart/**`; executor runs `go test -update`, the golden now encodes the bug, S1b characterization tests pass. The same holds for `__snapshots__/`, `*.snap`, `*.approved.txt`, `fixtures/*.json`. Also, ratchet's 'write the repro as tests/regress_<sig>' is undefined for a repro that is a shell `cmd/expect` (nothing in the zone's runner executes it).
findings.fix: Freeze by recorded file, not by glob: at the end of S4 (and S1b) red-proof.sh writes `contract.json.frozen[] = [{path, sha256}]` for every file the prober created or modified; gate.sh fails if any frozen path's blob at HEAD differs (`git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`), and guard-scope denies those exact paths in addition to globs. Ratchet appends the repro as a contract check `{id: regress_<sig>, kind: check, cmd, expect}` plus an optional zone-native test file, both added to `frozen[]`; gate.sh executes contract checks itself. Any diff hunk in files matching `*.snap|__snapshots__/**|*.golden|testdata/**|fixtures/**|*.approved.*|**/*.expected` sets `gate.json.checks.test_delta=true`, which blocks T0 auto-merge and is listed for S6. Add `fixture_globs[]` to the zones.json schema.

findings.section: §6 rows 14/17/19-20, §6 inputs I 'inspector verdict (max confirmed severity)', §3 S6 exit gate line 261, §4 inspect/blind schemas, §5.3
findings.claim: decide.sh has no matching row for a cold-lens UNSAFE (or customer FAIL) that carries neither repro nor hazard at T0/T1, the inspector verdict `I` is an agent-declared field rather than derived from findings, and three incompatible finding vocabularies make the table unimplementable as written.
findings.scenario: T1 unit: G=pass, S=yes, I=pass, Bc=PASS, Bk=UNSAFE with a prose finding (no repro ran, no hazard class), H=0, R=green, M=MATCH. Rows 1-13 do not apply; row 14 needs a repro; row 17 is defined for T2+ only; rows 19-20 need Bk ∈ {SAFE, skipped}; rows 21-22 do not apply → first-match-wins returns nothing, so the implementation's implicit default decides (MERGE ships the flagged change, ESCALATE spams H3). Second: sep-inspector returns `verdict: fix` with three `kind: note` findings; §3 says notes 'cannot block' but decide.sh consumes `I = fix` directly → row 10 → sendbacks.execute++ on an empty defect set → ratchet has no repro to write. Third: §5.3 uses block/hold/concern, §4 `kind` uses defect|hazard|note, §4 `severity` uses blocker|important|minor, §3 speaks of 'nits' and 'fix findings'; §3 names the file `inspect.json`, §4 `inspect-r<n>.json`; §3 field `note`, §4 `claim`; §4 `decision.json.inputs` omits L and E that §6 uses.
findings.fix: (1) decide.sh derives I, Bc-strength and Bk-strength from findings only: `block` ⇔ finding with `repro.ran==true`; `hold` ⇔ `hazard` set; everything else `concern`. An UNSAFE/FAIL verdict with neither is recorded as SAFE/PASS-with-concerns, routed to S9 and counted against that lens's precision (§11); the schema forbids `kind: block` without `repro.ran`. (2) Add row 14b: 'Bk=UNSAFE or Bc=FAIL with neither repro nor hazard → concern; if ≥2 lenses ran and they disagree → row 17 (any class), else continue'. (3) One vocabulary everywhere: `kind: block|hold|concern`, `severity: blocker|important|minor`, file `inspect-r<n>.json`, field `claim`, `decision.json.inputs = {G,S,I,Bc,Bk,M,H,K,R,L,E}`; update §3, §5.3, §6, §12.3 sep-defect-card accordingly. (4) Selftest feeds the T1 UNSAFE-no-repro fixture and asserts a row is hit.

findings.section: §7.4 narrative scan (line 499 'Hits in comments, test names …'), §3 S4 line 214 (`tests/acc_<u>.*`), §5.2 (`tests/regress_<sig>`), §6 row 5, §3 S5 neutral commits `<unit> change set <n>`
findings.claim: The leak-check greps the diff for unit ids including test names, but the spec mandates frozen files named after the unit id, so every unit's own acceptance test trips the narrative scan and the 'neutralize narrative' task cannot touch it; row 5 then escalates to INVALID → H3 on every unit.
findings.scenario: Unit id `U2`. Prober writes `tests/acc_U2.py` (frozen). Before S7, leak-scan greps the diff for `U2` → hit in the test filename → `narrative_terms:["U2"]` → executor receives 'neutralize narrative' → guard-scope denies editing/renaming a frozen test → S7 runs → `leak-check.json` dirty → row 5 rebuilds and re-runs S7 → dirty again → INVALID → H3 'harness problem'. Short ids (`U2`, `A1`) also false-positive on hex strings, `MENU2`, CSS class names. Rulings ids (`R14`) referenced by the prober in a test docstring produce the same dead end.
findings.fix: Name frozen artefacts by content, not by plan ids: `acc_<ac-id-lowercase>_<sha6>` and `regress_<sig6>` where sig is already a hash; exclude every `contract.json.frozen[]` path and its basename from the narrative grep; require epic/unit ids to be ≥8-char random tokens (e.g. `u-7f3ka2d9`) so a hit is unambiguous; run the narrative scan on the prober's output at S4 in `red-proof.sh` (a hit is a prober failure, exit 2) so narrative inside frozen files never reaches S7; the executor-side 'neutralize' task applies only to non-frozen paths.

findings.section: §3 S5 hooks line 229 ('unit id from `git branch --show-current`'), §12.4 line 745, §15 'unit from branch name', §3 S6 'worktree at the unit branch'; mechanics §9.4
findings.claim: The scope hook resolves the unit from a `sep/<epic>/<unit>` branch, but verified mechanics create workflow worktrees on `worktree-<runId>-<n>` and guard-bash forbids branch switching, so the hook either fails open (no enforcement) or fails closed (no executor can edit anything).
findings.scenario: sep-build.js spawns sep-executor with `isolation:'worktree'` → cwd `.claude/worktrees/<runId>-1`, branch `worktree-<runId>-1` (mechanics §9.4). First Edit → guard-scope runs `git branch --show-current` → `worktree-abc-1` → no `dag.json` unit matches. If the script treats 'unknown unit' as allow, writes[] and frozen tests are unenforced until the gate (and Bash `sed`/`mv` never were). If it treats it as deny, the executor cannot create a single file → SubagentStop `require-evidence.sh` fails 3× → status fail → exec_retries → S2 → H3, for every unit. The executor cannot fix it because guard-bash denies `git checkout/switch`. Separately, sep-inspector's worktree is created from session HEAD, not the unit branch, and `git checkout sep/<epic>/<unit>` is refused while the executor's worktree holds that branch ('already checked out at …').
findings.fix: Executor prompt step 1 (explicitly authorized): `git switch -c sep/<epic>/<unit>`; guard-bash allow-lists exactly `git switch -c sep/<epic>/<unit>` when the current branch matches `^worktree-` and denies all other branch ops; guard-scope FAILS CLOSED with reason 'branch not sep/*: run the branch step first' when the branch does not match `^sep/`; gate.sh/sandbox.sh locate the unit checkout with `git worktree list --porcelain` by branch, never by path. Inspector/verifier/judge worktrees use `git worktree add --detach <tmp> <head_sha>`. selftest.sh must exercise the hook inside a real `isolation:worktree` agent and assert both the deny-before-branch and allow-after-branch outcomes.

findings.section: §3 S5 line 240-241 (flake control), §3 S4 line 216 (red-proof flake wording), §5.2 ratchet
findings.claim: Quarantine-on-retry treats any intermittent failure as pre-existing flakiness, so a race introduced by the change — including one that makes the ratchet's permanent regression test flap — is merged instead of blocked; and the red-proof flake rule is written backwards.
findings.scenario: Executor adds a cache without a lock; `tests/regress_4f2a` (the permanent repro from round 1) now fails ~40% of runs. gate.sh: fails once → re-run 2× in isolation → passes → 'pass-on-retry → quarantined in ledger, not a block' → the unit merges with a race and the ratchet test that was supposed to make that defect impossible is silently disabled. Nothing downstream re-runs it 10×. Also §3 S4 reads 'passes on retry-in-isolation twice → not flaky' for a test that must be RED on base — implemented literally, red-proof accepts a test that passes on base.
findings.fix: A failing test may be quarantined only if it ALSO fails ≥1 of 3 runs on `base_sha` in the same environment (pre-existing flake); a test stable on base and unstable on HEAD is a block with `hazard: concurrency`, repro `{cmd, runs: "3/10 failed"}`. Acceptance tests (`frozen[]`), regress tests and contract checks are never quarantinable. Rewrite §3 S4 to 'fails on base on 2 further isolated runs (same exit class) → stable red'. Record quarantines in `gate.json.checks.flaky[]` with `{test, base_fail_rate, head_fail_rate}` so S9 can see divergence.

findings.section: §3 S6 exit gate line 259-261, §5.3 hazard classes, §6 row 19, §3 S1b observation-only units
findings.claim: Any important finding the inspector cannot execute here and that is not one of the seven hazard classes is forced to `note`, which cannot block, so real bugs in observation-only zones, infra-dependent paths, or classes outside the list merge through row 19 by design.
findings.scenario: Zone `reports` has `commands.test: null` and S1b produced only 3 golden cases; unit exports invoices to a partner SFTP. Inspector reads `datetime.now()` used where `invoice.issued_at` in the customer's timezone is required — wrong dates on every export. No harness exists to run it, SFTP is not reachable, timezone is not in {auth, data loss, migration, race, secrets, perf hot path, irreversible effect} → the finding must be `note` → row 19 MERGE (T1) with a DEFER list. Same for: a new dependency added by the executor that the prober never resolved, a JSON field whose meaning changed for external consumers, a connection leak on an error path.
findings.fix: Allow `hold` for important+ findings with `repro_blocked_by: env|data|infra|no-harness` plus a described `observation` step (§3 S1b already defines observation evidence); the one sep-verifier attempt then runs, and an unverified hold becomes a HOLD row exactly as today. Extend default `policy.hazard_classes` with: compatibility of public/serialized data, failure-path error handling, resource leaks, new third-party dependency, time/locale/encoding. In observation-only units treat an inspector `observation` (step + evidence file) as a repro-equivalent for routing to S5. Track `held_unverified→escape` in §11 so classes that never pay off are pruned.

findings.section: §12.2 sep-build.js sketch lines 704-716 (`rerun-blind`, `hold`, `ev.diff_sha256`), §5.4 counter reset, §4 evidence.json schema
findings.claim: The reference control flow re-runs the executor when it means to re-run S7, parks a unit whose hold was refuted, reads a field the evidence schema does not have, and resets every counter on each run, contradicting §5.4.
findings.scenario: (A) First leak-check dirty → `d.action==='rerun-blind'` → `round--; continue` → loop top calls sep-executor again with the same `cards=[]` → no new commits → `ev.diff_sha256 === st.lastHash` → `return {u, stuck:'no-progress'}` → unit parked; S7 is never re-run and the human gets a stuck card for a harness event. (B) Verifier REFUTES a hold → code falls through: `d.merge` is undefined, `d.action==='hold'` ≠ 'execute' → `return {u, sendback:'hold', why:d}` → parked with a nonsense target instead of merging. (C) `ev.diff_sha256` is not in §4 evidence.json (`{unit, head_sha, commands, files_touched, acceptance, zone_gates, status, attempt}`), so the no-progress check compares `undefined === null` and never fires, or always fires after a schema update. (D) `st` is created fresh per run; after an H3 resume `sendbacks.execute` restarts at 0 although §5.4 says only the named counter resets — bounded only by `human_escalations ≤ 3`, i.e. up to 3× the intended rounds.
findings.fix: Restructure the unit loop as an explicit state machine `phase ∈ {exec, gate, inspect, blind, decide}` where each decision action names the phase to re-enter (`rerun-blind` → `blind`, gate fail → `exec`); after a refuted hold set `H=0` and call `decide()` again; take `head_sha` from evidence.json and `diff_sha256` from gate.json (attested) for the no-progress check; read counters from `args.state` (the driver passes `state.json` in) and return the updated counters so `/sep` persists them; the H3 resume path passes `reset:[counterName]`. Add a selftest fixture that drives the sketch with a scripted 'dirty leak-check then clean' and 'hold then refuted' sequence and asserts S7 re-run and MERGE respectively.

findings.claim: The entire enforcement layer is specified as agent-frontmatter hooks plus a branch-name lookup, and the verified mechanics note says frontmatter hooks did not fire and workflow worktree branches are named `worktree-<runId>-<n>`, so blind-sandbox guards, executor stop gates, prober RED proof, pack-only reads and scope enforcement would all silently not run. Spec: "Hooks (`.claude/settings.json` global; agent-scoped ones live in frontmatter)" and "agent: sep-outsider-* | SubagentStart / PreToolUse / SubagentStop | assert-sandbox.sh / guard-blind.sh / check-evidence.sh + leak-scan.sh" (§12.4); "L3 primary: subagent `sep-outsider-*` with `omitClaudeMd: true`, no `memory`, frontmatter hooks: SubagentStart `assert-sandbox.sh` (refuses unless cwd is a manifest-verified sandbox)" (§7.3); "unit id from `git branch --show-current`" (§3 S5); §15 even records this as the resolution of "fragile `agent_type`/marker hooks". Note (claude-code-mechanics.md §9.3): "Agent frontmatter `hooks:` did NOT fire (tested PreToolUse/Bash with absolute and `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` paths ...). Do not rely on frontmatter hooks."; §9.2: "role-scoped enforcement lives in GLOBAL settings.json hooks that branch on `agent_type` and on `cwd`/branch, not in agent frontmatter"; §9.4: "branch `worktree-<runId>-<n>` created from the session HEAD"; §9.5–9.6: the headless `claude -p --restricted ... --agents ... --settings` launcher from a directory outside the project is what was verified to confine reads.
findings.scenario: sep-build.js runs `agent(blindPrompt(u,'cold'), {agentType:'sep-outsider-cold'})`. No SubagentStart/PreToolUse hook fires; the lens (tools Read/Grep/Glob/Bash; cwd = project root, because a workflow subagent cannot be started inside `blind/<u>/sandbox` — so even if `assert-sandbox.sh` did fire it would refuse every launch) reads `.separator/epics/<e>/units/<u>/card.md`. `reads.log` is never written because guard-blind.sh is what writes it, so `leak-check.forbidden_reads` is `[]`; the lens paraphrases the card without quoting `SEP-CANARY-…`, so `canary_hit=false`; L=clean, E non-empty → the "blind" verdict is counted and §7.2's "Blindness is auditable" is false. In the same run `require-evidence.sh` never blocks the executor, `red-proof.sh` never checks that the spike test fails on base, and `guard-scope.sh` in the executor's worktree reads branch `worktree-01ab-2`, not `sep/<epic>/<unit>` (and `git checkout` is denied by guard-bash), so it either denies every edit (unit parks after `exec_retries`) or, if written permissively, enforces nothing. Every "enforced" rule in §3 S5/S7 becomes a suggestion, which principle 14 names as the failure to avoid.
findings.fix: (1) Put every role hook in global `.claude/settings.json` behind one `sep-hook-router.sh` that reads `agent_type` and `cwd` from stdin and dispatches (`sep-executor` → guard-scope/guard-bash/require-evidence; `sep-prober` → red-proof; any `cwd` under `.separator/**/sandbox` → guard-blind/check-evidence/leak-scan), the path the mechanics note verified. (2) Launch blind lenses through the verified headless path from the sandbox directory (`claude -p --restricted --tools "Read,Grep,Glob,Bash" --allowedTools ... --agents blind-agents.json --agent sep-outsider-<lens> --settings blind-hooks.json --output-format json --json-schema ...`), invoked from `sandbox.sh`/`sep blind` inside a Bash call; make this the L3 primary and delete the frontmatter-hook subagent variant from §7.3/§12.1/§12.4. (3) Resolve the unit by cwd, not branch: the executor prompt's first authorized command is `git checkout -b sep/<epic>/<unit>` and guard-bash allows `git checkout -b sep/*` only while the current branch matches `^worktree-`; until then guard-scope reads a `dispatch.json {cwd → unit}` that the router writes on the executor's first SubagentStart. (4) `selftest.sh` asserts that a frontmatter-only hook does NOT fire and that the router does, so the assumption is tested rather than believed; rewrite the §15 line accordingly.

findings.claim: Every workflow call uses `agentType:'sep-*'` with no fallback, but the mechanics note shows custom agents written mid-session are not registered and an unknown agentType throws and kills the workflow; the spec's `/sep init` → shadow-mode flow never says "restart". Spec: "await agent(execPrompt(epic,u,cards,sha), {agentType:'sep-executor', ...})" (§12.2); "`/sep init` generates zones/policy/hooks/agents with conservative defaults ... the first 10 runs produce merge cards" (§11). Note (claude-code-mechanics.md §9.1): "Custom agents are registered only at session start. `.claude/agents/*.md` written mid-session are NOT visible to the Workflow `agentType` registry ... `agent(prompt,{agentType:'x'})` with an unknown type THROWS ... and kills the workflow unless caught ... workflow scripts must wrap agentType calls in try/catch and fall back ... installation docs must say 'restart Claude Code'."
findings.scenario: User runs `/sep init` then `/sep` in the same session. `sep-intake.js` executes `parallel([agent(..., {agentType:'sep-triage'}), agent(..., {agentType:'sep-intent-checker'})])`; the first call throws "agent type 'sep-triage' not found"; the run aborts before `triage.json` exists; `state.json` is never created; the user's first experience of the funnel is a stack trace and the shadow baseline (§11) never starts. The same crash recurs after any change that adds a role (e.g. an approved learner proposal adding a zone reviewer) until the session is restarted.
findings.fix: Add a `role(name, prompt, opts)` helper to every script: try `agentType:name`; on the specific "not found" error fall back to the default agent with the prefix "Your complete role card is `.claude/agents/<name>.md`; read it first and obey its tools list", and log `fallback:true` into `metrics.jsonl`. Forbid the fallback for roles whose isolation is load-bearing (`sep-outsider-*`, `sep-intent-checker`, `sep-plan-auditor`) — those run through the headless launcher (finding 1), which loads `--agents` from a JSON file and is registry-independent. `/sep init` and the §13 install step print "restart Claude Code to register agents"; `selftest.sh` probes one `agent({agentType:'sep-verifier'})` and records `agents_registered` in `selftest.json`; `gate.sh` refuses auto-merge while it is false.

findings.claim: The acceleration argument rests on numbers the notes do not contain or contradict. Spec: "PRIORS consistent with published self-approval rates (5–47%)" — no note has a self-approval rate; the nearest figures are reward-hack rates on hack-prone tasks (failure-modes.md F4: "Claude Sonnet 3.7 classifier hack rate 44% / hidden-test hack rate 23% ... Sonnet 4 fails the holdout tests 5%"), a different quantity. Spec: "one **call** = one fresh subagent invocation (parallelizable, ~1–3 min)" vs anthropic-agents.md F4 "QA rounds of ~9 min / ~$3 each" and review-judging.md src 2 Code Review "~20 min, $15-25 per PR". Spec: "8 independent T1 units ≈ 1–2 chain lengths" vs mechanics §9.7 "4 CPUs → at most 2 concurrent workflow agents per workflow". Spec: "Token cost is 2–4× a chat on T0–T2" vs anthropic-agents.md F3 (single agents "about 4x" a chat, multi-agent "about 15x") and decomposition.md src 3 ("3-10x more tokens than single-agent"). Spec: "first-attempt `p = 0.45`" while §11 targets "S5 ≥ 85%" and decomposition.md F17 says units should be sized so the agent "finishes with ~80%+ reliability". The notes' own verdict is the opposite of the section's tone: "Net acceleration of a heavy funnel is unproven" (failure-modes.md Q7) and METR's "developers took 19% longer with AI" on large familiar repos (F15) appears nowhere in the spec.
findings.scenario: A steady-state T1 unit runs triage → spike → executor → gate → inspector → sandbox → two lenses → integrate, each a serial dependency. At the notes' observed 9–20 min per execute/review-class call the wall clock is roughly 60–100 min plus queueing behind the 2-agent harness cap; the straight-line chat the user does today is ~15 min plus two touches. §10 nevertheless prints "8.3 vs 27.2" and "net faster", so the user (hard requirement 2 = acceleration) adopts the funnel on T1 and experiences exactly the METR perception gap the notes warn about: slower in fact, believed faster, with `p=0.45` implying ~1 rework round per unit that the FPY target says should not exist.
findings.fix: (a) Delete the "(5–47%)" citation or replace it with what the notes support and what it measures ("reward-hack rates on hack-prone tasks 1–44% by model generation; recall of injected errors 22–29% per reviewer; no published straight-line escape rate"). (b) Make `p` consistent with S2's sizing goal: show two rows, `p=0.85` (target; units sized per the 80% horizon) and `p=0.45` (pessimistic), and state that measured FPY(S5) < 0.7 means "units too large", not "more review". (c) Replace "~1–3 min" with a per-stage latency budget column (execute 10–20 min, lens 5–10 min, gate = `suite_seconds`) and compute the parallel line with `min(wave, harness_cap)`; here that is 2, so "8 units ≈ 4 chain lengths". (d) Re-state tokens as "3–10× a single agent (notes), i.e. 10–40× a chat" alongside the user's explicit acceptance of tokens. (e) Cite METR as the reason the shadow baseline measures wall clock rather than self-report, and make "funnel ≤ baseline by unit 20" a gating condition for leaving shadow mode, not only a metric row.

findings.section: §3 S5 gate (lines 242–243), §5.3 (line 405), §4 gate.json (line 359)
findings.claim: The gate auto-quarantines any test that passes on re-run, which the verification notes explicitly forbid, hiding the concurrency bugs that §5.3 itself lists as a hazard class. Spec: "flake control (a failing test re-run 2× in isolation; pass-on-retry → quarantined in ledger, not a block)". Note (verification-tech.md F20): "the gate re-runs a failed test once *only if* it is tagged flaky, never silently for others"; "false reds erode trust in the gate and teach the agent to 'just rerun' or to weaken tests"; flakes are to be discovered by a nightly rerun "3–5× on unchanged main", not at the gate.
findings.scenario: A T1 unit adds a background worker; its acceptance test `acc_u3` fails one run in three because the new code has a real race. `gate.sh` sees the failure, re-runs it 2× in isolation (single test, no contention) → passes → `gate.json.checks.flaky:[acc_u3]`, `pass:true`. S6 sees a note, not a blocker; S7's customer lens runs the AC once and it passes; row 20 → MERGE to integration → main at H4. The race ships, and the only test that would have caught it is now quarantined, so the escape is never attributed to the unit and the zone floor never rises.
findings.fix: Only tests already listed in `zones.json.flaky[]` (populated by a nightly `sep flaky` job that reruns the suite 3–5× on unchanged `integration`, as the note describes) may be re-run at the gate. A new intermittent failure in a test the unit added or touched, or in any test that has never flipped on base, is `G=fail` with a defect card `kind: hazard, class: concurrency` (so it takes the §5.3 HOLD path if the executor cannot reproduce it deterministically). Pre-existing untagged failures are re-run 3× on `base_sha`, not on the branch, and quarantined only if they flip there too.

findings.section: §2.1 (lines 112–115), §3 S5 gate (lines 238–245), §4 zones.json (lines 344–347), §3 S6 (line 257)
findings.claim: Security review exists only as an S7 "security lens" at T3 (~5% of units) and the mechanical gate has a secrets scan but no SAST command, although the notes document security defects as a large, model-independent fraction of AI code and prescribe SAST in the deterministic gate. Spec: T3 row "as T2 + security lens"; gate: "secrets scan of the diff clean"; zones `commands:{setup,build,test,fast,lint,run,mutate,smoke}` (no security command). Note (failure-modes.md F16): "AI-generated code introduced risky security flaws in 45% of tests ... XSS (CWE-80) missed in 86% of relevant samples ... security pass rates 'remained essentially flat, hovering between 45% and 55% regardless of model generation'. Implication: an outside reviewer with a security lens plus SAST in the deterministic gate; do not expect model upgrades to fix this class." verification-tech.md F13: Semgrep in PR mode "will only report issues introduced by that pull request"; quality-systems.md src 25: Anthropic's own SDLC runs "deterministic SAST".
findings.scenario: T1 unit, one zone `web/`, 2 files, not a risk path: it renders a user-supplied `display_name` into an HTML template without escaping. Gate: tests green, lint green, no SAST. S6 (single correctness/contract lens at T1) confirms the contract. S7 customer lens verifies "WHEN a user sets a display name THE SYSTEM SHALL show it on the profile" → PASS; cold lens → SAFE. Row 20 → MERGE; H4 promotes. A stored XSS reaches main through every stage by design, and `escapes/100 merged` stays at 0 until a user reports it.
findings.fix: Add `commands.sast` to `zones.json` (cartographer infers `semgrep ci --baseline-commit <base_sha>` with the language's default ruleset, or CodeQL/Bandit/gosec/etc. where present; `null` is legal and, like `test:null`, degrades to an `observation` and raises the class by one for any unit whose write-set touches input handling, templates, SQL or auth). `gate.sh` runs it diff-scoped at every class; a high-severity finding on a changed line is `G=fail` with a built-in repro (rule id + file:line). Add a fixed hazard-prompt block to the S6 lens at T1+ ("user input reaching HTML/SQL/shell/deserialization/auth decisions → hazard class"), not only the T3 security lens.

findings.section: §3 S4 (line 219), §2.1 T1 row (line 113), §3 S5 hooks (lines 230–231), §12.1 sep-planner (line 664), §4 contract.json (lines 353–354)
findings.claim: For the steady-state majority of work (T1, `unknowns == []`, declared zone) S4 is skipped and "the planner's contract `check` is the gate", but the planner cannot write repo tests (tools `Write(.separator/epics/**)` only), so the acceptance test is written by the executor after the code and the RED-on-base proof the spec elsewhere calls "the deliverable" never happens. Note (hypothesis.md F5): "Verify RED (Mandatory) ... If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing"; anti-pattern 5: "Tests-after pass immediately (proving nothing)"; failure-modes.md F4: "An implementer that can see and edit all tests is grading its own exam"; verification-tech.md F6: a fix is accepted only if "FAIL_TO_PASS tests (failing before the patch) now pass".
findings.scenario: T1 request "add a `--json` flag to `export`". The planner writes contract check `pytest tests/test_export.py::test_json_flag`; the test does not exist; S4 is skipped. The card must declare `test_writes` or guard-scope denies the executor the `test_globs` path. The executor writes the test and the code in one session; the test asserts what the code produces and passes immediately; `contract.json.red_evidence` is never populated. Gate green, S6 sees an internally consistent test, S7 customer lens PASS. Later, §3 S3's "RED-on-base check is re-run" compares against a red run that never happened. A wrong-but-self-consistent implementation (e.g. `--json` printing the pretty table wrapped in a JSON string) merges with the ratchet's premise broken for half of all units.
findings.fix: When S4 is skipped, `gate.sh pre` (0 calls, seconds) executes every contract `check` on `base_sha` and requires a nonzero exit, writing `red_evidence`; a check that cannot fail on base (missing test file, command not found) routes the unit to S4 after all (one bounded prober call) — or let the planner author the acceptance test text under `.separator/epics/<e>/units/<u>/tests/` (a path it may already write), which `pack.sh` copies into the worktree as frozen `tests/acc_*` before the executor starts, then `gate.sh pre` proves RED. Restrict `test_writes` to non-acceptance tests.

findings.section: §6 inputs (lines 431–432) and row 16 (line 453), §7.6 (lines 514–516), §12.1 sep-judge (line 673)
findings.claim: The MATCH/MISMATCH intent comparison is a single low-effort LLM judgment that can defer a merge and, on repeat, escalate to a human, contradicting the notes on judge variance and on forced reasoning before verdicts. Spec: "M intent match (cold `inferred_intent` vs ACCEPTANCE, judged by `sep-judge` low effort, MATCH|MISMATCH)"; row 16: "Bk = ILLEGIBLE or M = MISMATCH, no other finding | DEFER-GATE | S5 'add rationale' ... once; second time → H3 (design problem)" (§12.1 lists sep-judge as "inherit / high", so the effort level is also internally inconsistent). Note (review-judging.md F5): "repeated identical pairwise judgments flip 13.6% on average; 28% of questions >20% flip ... semantically equivalent templates change the majority verdict in 25% of cases; 11 trials needed"; anti-pattern 5: "a single pairwise verdict is not evidence"; F7: "generating a long Chain-of-Thought before evaluation effectively reduce[s] the harmful self-preference" → rule 8/F7 "force long reasoning before verdict"; F12: the final verdict "is computed by a rule ... not by asking the same LLM 'so, overall, accept?'".
findings.scenario: A correct T1 unit. The cold lens writes "adds a percentage discount to cart totals"; ACCEPTANCE A1 says "WHEN a valid code is entered at checkout THE SYSTEM SHALL reduce the total by the code's percentage". The low-effort judge, one sample, returns MISMATCH ("cart" ≠ "checkout"). Row 16 → a fresh executor is dispatched to "add rationale" → new diff → S6 delta + new sandbox + two lenses (3–4 calls). The second judgment is another single sample with a 13–25% chance of MISMATCH → H3 "design problem": a human touch on a correct change. Over 30 T1 units this yields several spurious rounds and at least one stuck card, all charged to `sendbacks.execute`.
findings.fix: Make M an absolute per-AC check: the judge (normal effort, reasoning before verdict) marks each AC `covered | not_covered | unclear` against the inferred intent; run 3 samples with the two texts in alternating order and take the majority; MISMATCH = any AC `not_covered` by majority. A MISMATCH with no other finding is a `concern` (logged for S9, shown on the card) unless it coincides with ILLEGIBLE from the same lens or the unit is T2+; and the first DEFER-GATE consumes no S6/S7 re-run when the resulting diff is comment-only (script-verified via `git diff -w` on non-comment tokens).

findings.section: §3 S4 (lines 211–212), §3 S2 (line 177), §12.1 sep-designer (line 666)
findings.claim: The spike judge "picks" among 2–3 alternative spikes and two judges pick among three same-model designs, with no absolute rubric, no order swap and no distinct designer mandates — the pairwise-preference setup the notes show is position-biased and error-correlated. Spec: "for architectural unknowns run 2–3 alternative spikes in parallel and let a fresh judge pick"; "three `sep-designer` agents (independent, cannot see each other) + 2 judges → `design/chosen.md` → H1". Note (review-judging.md F5): "position bias not random; strongly affected by the quality gap between candidates" and "(a) prefer ABSOLUTE grading ... (b) When a pairwise comparison is unavoidable ... run both orderings and treat disagreement as a tie, or randomize order across k>=3 trials"; failure-modes.md F13: preferences reverse on reordering "at rates of 25%, 58%, and 89%"; review-judging.md F10: "3 independent agents made identical errors"; hypothesis.md F9: the feature-dev plugin's panel uses "2-3 code-architect agents with different focuses (minimal / clean / pragmatic)".
findings.scenario: T3 epic (new billing zone). Three sep-designer agents with the same prompt produce three near-identical designs sharing one wrong assumption (the ORM supports the migration primitive they all rely on). Both judges read them in the order 1,2,3 and both prefer design 1; `chosen.md` shows "2/2 judges" and H1's human approves what looks like consensus. S4's spike later refutes the shared assumption → S2 send-back (`sendbacks.decompose` cap 1) → H3. The panel cost five calls and a human touch and filtered nothing.
findings.fix: Give designers distinct mandates (minimal-change / clean-architecture / pragmatic-reuse) so their errors decorrelate; judges score every candidate independently against an absolute binary checklist derived from ACCEPTANCE, hazard classes and known constraints (reasoning first, `unknown` allowed), each judge seeing candidates in a different random order; a candidate is chosen only if it leads both judges' absolute scores, otherwise H1 receives the two leaders with the disagreement shown. For S4, rank spikes by `spike.json` evidence (claims supported/refuted, cost) and let the judge only break ties, never express a preference without citing a refuted claim.

findings.section: §3 S5 exit gate (line 238), §12.2 sketch (lines 705–706, 709), §12.2 prose (lines 688–689)
findings.claim: The "MECHANICAL GATE (code, `gate.sh`, writes `gate.json` which agents cannot write)" is, in the reference implementation, a low-effort LLM agent that runs `gate.sh` and returns JSON the script trusts unverified, and the sketch dereferences that result without a null check. Spec: "const gate = await agent(`Run .separator/bin/gate.sh ${epic} ${u.id}; return gate.json`, {agentType:'sep-verifier', schema:GATE, effort:'low'}); if (!gate.pass) {...}"; "Scripts have no filesystem access: agents write artifacts, scripts hold counters". Note (review-judging.md F14): "'20-30% of subagent reports contain at least one claim that doesn't match the underlying tool output' ... the orchestrator should verify subagent claims against tool output ... with deterministic checks where possible"; verification-tech.md anti-pattern 4: "Trusting exit codes without reading the report"; anthropic-agents.md F13: "agent() resolves to null on stop/API error".
findings.scenario: (a) Zone `full` takes 8 minutes; the small/low verifier hits its turn cap or the API errors → `agent()` returns null → `gate.pass` throws TypeError → `sep-build.js` aborts mid-wave with `state.json` unchanged, and resume replays the same crash. (b) The verifier runs `gate.sh`, one test fails, and at low effort it returns `{pass:true}` paraphrased from stdout it skimmed; `decide()` sends a red unit into S6, S7 and integration (4+ calls) before the pre-push hash check notices anything — and that hook only checks that code did not change after the verdict, not that the gate was green.
findings.fix: Run `gate.sh` from a deterministic hook (the global SubagentStop router for `agent_type == sep-executor` from finding 1; the spec already runs the fast gate there) so `gate.json` is written by a script; have `gate.sh` also write `gate.sig = sha256(gate.json || key)` with a key created by `selftest.sh` and denied to worker roles by guard-scope; make the workflow's verifier step "print gate.json and gate.sig" and have `decide()` recompute the signature and compare `gate.json.head_sha` with `evidence.head_sha` before using any field; null or invalid → `G=fail` with `harness:true`, never a crash; the pre-push/CI `separator-gate` verifies the same signature.

findings.section: §7.4 (lines 498–502), §12.2 order (lines 708–710), §3 S8 (lines 294–295), §6 inputs (lines 430–434: no hash-equality input)
findings.claim: The "neutralize narrative" task edits the unit after S6 has passed it, and the decision table then combines S6's verdict on the old diff with S7's on the new one, contradicting the approvals-expire-on-change rule the notes take from branch protection and that the spec applies only at S8. Spec: "the executor is sent a 'neutralize narrative' task (free, no round charged) before S7 runs"; sketch order: inspector → `sandbox.sh` → blind; "code changed after the verdict invalidates the verdict" (S8 only). Note (quality-systems.md F8): GitHub "dismiss stale pull request approvals when commits are pushed that affect the diff" → "Any new commit after a pass invalidates the pass"; anti-pattern 4: "Approvals that survive new commits - the classic 'fixed one thing after approval' leak"; failure-modes.md F7: removing the explicit scope sentence "raised the measured overeager rate on Claude Code from 0.0% to 17.1%".
findings.scenario: A unit passes S6 (`inspect-r1.json` for diff hash H1). `leak-scan` finds the epic id in a test name. A fresh sep-executor receives "neutralize narrative" — a task with no card, no write-set statement and no evidence requirement — renames the test and, over-eagerly, also "fixes" an off-by-one it notices next to it → hash H2 (guard-scope permits it: same write-set). S7 runs on H2 and passes. `decide()` merges I(H1) with B(H2) → MERGE; `decision.json.diff_sha256 = H2`; the pre-push check sees no change after the verdict. The un-inspected edit ships.
findings.fix: Run the narrative grep inside `gate.sh` before S6 (it is a grep over the diff and the per-epic term list), so neutralization happens before any verdict exists; implement neutralization as a script (`redact.sh --narrative` rewriting only matched tokens, then re-running the fast gate) or, if an agent must do it, give it a card whose write-set is the matched lines only and re-run S6 in delta mode afterwards; add `head_sha` to `inspect-r<n>.json`, the blind `manifest.json` and `evidence.json`, make `decide()` require all three equal (else RE-RUN the stale stage), and add that equality to `selftest.sh`.

value.reasoning:
Facts check out. code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md (fetched today): "Subagent worktrees use the same base branch as --worktree, so they branch from your repository's default branch unless worktree.baseRef is set to "head""; "You can't set worktree.baseRef to a branch name. To start a worktree from a specific existing branch, create it with git directly"; branch is `worktree-<name>`; a worktree with changes is kept. Mechanics finding 4 saw "from session HEAD" only because that test repo had no remote (docs: fallback to local HEAD when origin/HEAD is unavailable); this project HAS `origin`, so in the smoke test every `isolation: worktree` agent starts from origin/HEAD, not from `claude/pensive-knuth-lvfjko` or `integration`. The "already used by worktree" refusal reproduced locally (git 2.43): `git worktree add ../w2 sep/E/U3` and `git checkout sep/E/U3` from another worktree both exit 128.

Spec does not handle it. §8.2 literally claims "`isolation: worktree`, branch `sep/<epic>/<unit>` from `base_sha`"; §S5/§12.4/§15 derive the unit from `git branch --show-current`; no `checkout`/`worktree add` step exists anywhere in SPEC.md, S3 is "pure code, 0 calls" and "scripts have no filesystem access", so nobody in the spec creates the unit branch. As written, wave-2 units start without wave-1 work (H4 promotes integration→main only at cadence, so integration ≠ main most of the time), commits land on `worktree-<runId>-<n>` where `sep-integrator` cannot find them, and guard-scope sees no unit.

But the proposed fix is not the right one.
