(2) Dropping `isolation: worktree` loses the platform-enforced edit/cwd/git-redirect isolation, and since agent-thread Bash cwd resets between calls, an executor that once forgets `cd $WORKTREE` runs tests or `git commit` in the main checkout. (3) The claim "cannot give an executor a worktree on sep/<epic>/<unit> from base_sha" is true of the platform feature but false as a blocker: a linked worktree can check out any commit, and the drafted `.separator/bin/sep.cjs unit start` (line 350) already does `git checkout -b sep/<e>/<u> <base_sha>` (or `checkout` if it exists) inside the auto worktree and writes `.sep-role`, which cures the wrong base and the branch-name problem after the executor's first command. What remains genuinely broken, in spec and draft alike, is the collision: every retry (`exec_retries`) and every S6/S7→S5 round is a NEW agent → new auto worktree, while the previous attempt's worktree (kept, it has commits) still holds `sep/<e>/<u>` → `git checkout` refused → executor dies at step 1 → S2/H3. Same for `sep-inspector` "worktree at the unit branch". Severity lowered to major: the spec text must be corrected and ~5 lines added to `unit start`; no redesign, no loss of any funnel property.
value.better_fix: Keep `isolation: worktree` (frontmatter AND pass `isolation:'worktree'` in the workflow `agent()` options, since frontmatter-via-agentType is untested) and rewrite the spec to say the truth: the auto worktree's initial base and its `worktree-<name>` branch are irrelevant; the unit branch is established by the executor's mandatory first command `sep unit start <epic> <unit>` (script, inside the worktree), which: (a) runs `git worktree list --porcelain`; if `refs/heads/sep/<epic>/<unit>` is held by another worktree (the previous attempt's), `git worktree unlock` (ignore error) + `git worktree remove --force` it — safe because `unit finish` commits everything and notes live in `.separator/`; (b) `git checkout -b sep/<epic>/<unit> <base_sha>` or `git checkout sep/<epic>/<unit>`; (c) writes `.sep-role {epic, unit, role, worktree}`; (d) runs zone `commands.setup` if declared (a worktree is a fresh checkout). Hooks in GLOBAL settings.json (not frontmatter) branch on stdin `agent_type` and read `.sep-role` from stdin `cwd`; no `.sep-role` yet → deny edits (fail-closed). Fix §8.2, §S5 hooks, §12.4 and §15 line 873 accordingly ("unit from `.sep-role` in cwd; branch name is only checked to equal sep/<epic>/<unit>"). sep-inspector: `git checkout --detach sep/<epic>/<unit>` (never the branch itself); sep-prober: same protocol on `spike/<epic>/<unit>` from `base_sha`, script copies the test out and removes the worktree. Corollary of the same git rule: `sep merge` must not assume `integration` is checkout-free — locate the worktree holding it (`git worktree list --porcelain`) and merge there, or refuse with a clear message if the human's main checkout sits on it. Optional policy for very large repos: `policy.worktree_mode: "persistent"` = the finding's `git worktree add -B ... <base_sha>` reused across attempts to avoid re-checkout/re-setup, still with `.sep-role`-based hooks.

value.reasoning:
Factual core verified against the official worktrees doc (fetched today): `worktree.baseRef` accepts only "fresh"|"head"; "You can't set worktree.baseRef to a branch name"; subagent `isolation: worktree` uses the same base and an auto-named `worktree-<name>` branch; "fresh" fetches origin/HEAD and falls back to local HEAD only when origin/HEAD is absent (which is why the mechanics doc §9.4 saw "from session HEAD" in this remote-less repo; in the user's real repos it will be origin/main). So `isolation: worktree` alone never yields `sep/<epic>/<unit>` from `base_sha`, and the spec (§8.2, §12.1, §12.4 "unit from branch name", §15 traceability) writes as if it did: no step in S3/S5/§12.2 puts the worktree on the unit branch, and S5's guard-bash "deny branch switching" would block the checkout that is needed. The spec does NOT handle it.

But half of the scenario is over-claimed. Inside an isolation worktree, `git checkout -b sep/<e>/<u> <base_sha>` is a local git op that Claude Code permits (docs: only edits/cwd/git redirected INTO the main checkout are blocked; mechanics §9.4: "the agent can run local git commands inside it"). The reference implementation already built in /home/user/---/.separator/bin/sep.cjs does exactly this in `sep unit start` (lines 347-352: `git checkout -q -b sep/<e>/<u> <card.base_sha>`, writes `.sep-role`), and `unitContext()` (line 130) reads `.sep-role` first, then the branch name — so "wrong base" and "guard-scope gets worktree-bright-fox" are a one-command bootstrap, not a design impossibility. "Scope guard void" is also overstated: S5 states the mechanical gate (`git diff base..HEAD ⊆ writes[]`) is authoritative and hooks are fast-fail. The wave-2 base is already covered at design level by S3/§8.5/§8.7 (base re-stamped to the integration tip, RED-on-base re-run, remaining branches rebased) — the current sep.cjs stamps `card.base_sha` from the epic base only (line 329) and never advances it, which is an implementation gap independent of `isolation: worktree`.
